# Maps as files

A map is one file, `<name>.snmap`, and optionally a definition in the content.
The server is started with the file, loads it and serves it. Each client
fetches it before it draws anything. Making a map changes no engine code.

The proving ground is the map a server runs when it is given none. The server
writes it into the same format in memory, from the functions in
`shared/world/proving.ts`, and loads it through the same reader. A test holds
the two equal: every height, every static piece in its slot, and all 6,144 node
slots (`tests/integration/maps.test.ts`).

## Make one

A map is built from a folder of plain layers by `tools/map.ts`. The quickest
start is the proving ground's own folder:

```sh
bun tools/map.ts proving var/proving.snmap           # the proving ground as a file
bun tools/map.ts unpack var/proving.snmap var/mine   # its folder of layers
# change the layers, and the id in map.json
bun tools/map.ts build var/mine var/mine.snmap       # the folder as a map
bun tools/map.ts info var/mine.snmap                 # what a file holds
bun server/main.ts --dev --map var/mine.snmap
```

`build` and `info` print the map's id, hash, size, counts, and any content id
it names that the core pack lacks. `build` refuses a folder that would not
play, and says why: a missing layer, a picture of the wrong size or depth, a
spawn point off the map, more than 256 node slots in a chunk.

Unpacking a map and building the folder again gives the same bytes.

## A folder of layers

A chunk is 64 m and the ground has a sample every 2 m, edges included. A map
of 8 chunks a side is 512 m and 257 samples a side.

Pictures are north up, as the map screen shows them. The first pixel is the
north-west corner, which is the highest x and the highest z. Places in the JSON
files are in metres from the map's south-east corner: x grows west and z grows
north, since east is -x. A yaw is in degrees from north, turning toward +x.

| File | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `map.json` | `{ "id": "core:miami", "chunks": [125, 125], "minY": -32, "stepY": 0.00390625, "seaLevel": 0 }`. The id is the map's name to the server and to saves, and the id of its definition if it has one: 1 to 64 plain characters with no space. A height is `minY + value * stepY` metres, so 16 bits at 1/256 m reach 256 m above `minY`. Without `seaLevel` the map has no water |
| `heights.png` | 16-bit greyscale, a pixel a sample. Or `heights.u16`: the same values in the same order, little-endian, with no header |
| `tint.png` | 8-bit, greyscale or indexed, a pixel a sample: its palette index (`shared/pack/palette.ts`). Or `tint.u8`. Without either, index 0 everywhere |
| `statics.json` | `[{ "kind": "core:wall", "x": 240.5, "y": 1.8, "z": 270, "yaw": 90 }]`. Pieces set down with the world and owned by nobody, by content id and centre. They snap to 1/512 m. Optional |
| `nodes.json` | Layers of resource nodes, described below. Optional |
| `spawns.json` | `[{ "name": "Plaza", "x": 256, "z": 240, "yaw": 0 }]`. 1 to 16. The first is where a new survivor arrives, and a dead one chooses among them |

A PNG must be one channel and not interlaced. `unpack` writes `tint.png` indexed
with the game's palette, so it shows in its colours.

### Resource nodes

A chunk has at most 256 node slots, and a node is known by its chunk and slot,
in saves too. `nodes.json` is a list of layers. A chunk's slots are the first
layer's, then the next's, so adding a layer at the end or a node at the end of
a list leaves the others where they were.

```json
[
  { "seed": 7, "perChunk": 96, "kinds": { "core:tree": 5, "core:rock": 3 }, "allow": "woods.png" },
  { "list": [{ "kind": "core:rock", "x": 12.5, "z": 40, "yaw": 0 }] }
]
```

- **A scattered layer** puts `perChunk` slots in every chunk at places a hash
  of the seed gives. Each holds a kind drawn by weight. A slot stays empty
  where the ground is under 0.3 m above the sea or steeper than about 32
  degrees, and where `allow` is darker than half. `allow` is an 8-bit greyscale
  picture of the whole map at 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 or 64 m a pixel. Without it a
  node may stand anywhere. Two layers with different pictures put trees in the
  woods and rocks on the hills. The proving ground has 96 slots a chunk, and
  2,658 of its 6,144 hold a node.
- **A listed layer** stands each node on the ground where it says, to
  1/1024 m. A slot is a node's place among those of its chunk, in the order
  listed.

A kind the content lacks is left out, and in a scattered layer the others share
its slots.

## The definition

The file is the ground. What lives on it is content: a definition of type
`map` whose id is the file's (`MapDef` in `shared/content/defs.ts`). It goes
among the definitions the server and the page compile. Today those are the
core pack's (`content/core.ts`), so the id begins `core:`.

```ts
{ id: "core:miami", type: "map", chunks: [125, 125], seaLevel: 0, zones: [
  { kind: "spawn", at: [4100, 3900], radius: 60 },
  { kind: "spawn", at: [4100, 4400], half: [80, 20] },
] }
```

- `chunks`, and `seaLevel` if given, must be the file's. A server refuses to
  start on a pair that disagree.
- A zone is a circle of `radius` metres around `at`, or with `half` a box of
  that half width and half depth.
- Creatures do not yet spawn by region. Until they do, a new world's herd
  starts in the first zone of kind `spawn` and its hunters in the last. A map
  with no definition, or no spawn zone, starts with no creatures, and the
  server says so as it starts.
- `label`, `game` and what a zone names (`spawns`, `crate`) are checked and not
  yet read.

The proving ground's definition is in `server/world.ts`: its id, `proving:1`,
is the one saves already carry, and is no pack's.

## Run one

`--map <file>` starts a server on that file. Without it the map is the proving
ground.

A save records the id and the hash of the map it was made on. A server refuses
to load a save onto a map of another id, or onto other bytes of the same map,
and names both hashes. `--allow-map-mismatch` loads it anyway, and from its
next commit the save is that map's. What was built stays at its coordinates,
and a used-up node stays used up by chunk and slot, so both are only right on
the new map if its ground and nodes are where the old one's were. A save from
before maps were files has no hash and takes the hash of the map of its id.

Any change to a map's file changes its hash, a moved spawn point included.

## How it reaches a client

- `/map.json` answers `{ "id", "hash", "file" }`.
- `file` is `map.<first 16 hex digits of the file's SHA-256>.snmap`, served
  compressed and marked never to change, so a browser fetches a map once.
- The page fetches both while it fetches its assets, reads the file, and makes
  the renderer from it. The welcome carries the map's id and hash as before, and
  a client whose file has another id or hash closes the connection. No wire
  message changed.
- A page refuses a map with more samples a side than the device's largest
  texture.

Anything that plays without a browser does the same two fetches and calls
`parseMap`, `mapHeightfield` and `mapNodes` (`shared/world/mapfile.ts`), as
`tests/fixtures/net.ts` does.

## The file

Little-endian. The layout is the header comment of `shared/world/mapfile.ts`,
which is the reference. In short:

| Part | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| Header | `SNMP`, version 1, the hash, chunks along x and z, the 2 m cell, `minY`, `stepY`, `seaLevel`, the id |
| `HGTS` | A u16 a sample, each less what its left, upper and upper-left neighbours predict |
| `TINT` | A u8 a sample |
| `STAT` | A table of content ids, then 16-byte rows: id, yaw, x, y, z in 1/512 m |
| `NODE` | One layer of nodes: scattered (seed, slots a chunk, weighted kinds, a bit per square of where they may stand) or listed (per chunk, 7-byte rows) |
| `SPWN` | Name, x, z, yaw for each spawn point |

The hash is FNV-1a over every byte after it, and is the number the welcome has
always carried. A reader skips a section whose tag it does not know. A file
that is damaged, of another version, or unplayable is refused with the reason.

Heights are stored as differences so that the file compresses. The proving
ground is 233 KB and travels as 38 KB. A generated map of rolling ground, 127
chunks a side (8,128 m, 4,065 samples a side), is 49.7 MB and 4.9 MB
compressed. It was written in 0.11 s and read in 0.09 s, in one run on the
development machine while other work ran.

## Limits

These are left for the world-building project.

| Limit | Why |
| --- | --- |
| A map is 63 chunks a side (4,032 m) on every device, and 127 (8,128 m) on one with 4,096-pixel textures | The ground is one texture and the whole grid is held in memory. There is no terrain streaming. 128 chunks is 4,097 samples, one too many |
| Samples are 2 m apart | The terrain tiles are built for that spacing |
| One palette index a sample | There are no terrain textures |
| Statics are pieces of content: boxes, at most 65,535 a chunk, sent to clients as rows | There are no mesh colliders |
| Zones only place a new world's creatures | Spawn tables and loot tables are stubs |
| The whole file is fetched and read before the first frame | No part of a map is streamed |

# Maps as files

A map is one file, `<name>.snmap`, and optionally a definition in the content.
The server is started with the file, loads it and serves it. Each client
fetches it before it draws anything. Making a map changes no engine code.

The proving ground is the map a server runs when it is given none. The server
writes it into the same format in memory, from the functions in
`shared/world/proving.ts`, and loads it through the same reader. A test holds
the two equal: every height, every static piece in its slot, and all 6,144 node
slots (`tests/integration/maps.test.ts`).

## Make one

A map is built from a folder of plain layers by `tools/map.ts`. The quickest
start is the proving ground's own folder:

```sh
bun tools/map.ts proving var/proving.snmap           # the proving ground as a file
bun tools/map.ts unpack var/proving.snmap var/mine   # its folder of layers
# change the layers, and the id in map.json
bun tools/map.ts build var/mine var/mine.snmap       # the folder as a map
bun tools/map.ts info var/mine.snmap                 # what a file holds
bun server/main.ts --dev --map var/mine.snmap
```

`build` and `info` print the map's id, hash, size, counts, and any content id
it names that the core pack lacks. `build` refuses a folder that would not
play, and says why: a missing layer, a picture of the wrong size or depth, a
spawn point off the map, more than 256 node slots in a chunk.

Unpacking a map and building the folder again gives the same bytes.

## A folder of layers

A chunk is 64 m and the ground has a sample every 2 m, edges included. A map
of 8 chunks a side is 512 m and 257 samples a side.

Pictures are north up, as the map screen shows them. The first pixel is the
north-west corner, which is the highest x and the highest z. Places in the JSON
files are in metres from the map's south-east corner: x grows west and z grows
north, since east is -x. A yaw is in degrees from north, turning toward +x.

| File | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `map.json` | `{ "id": "core:miami", "chunks": [125, 125], "minY": -32, "stepY": 0.00390625, "seaLevel": 0 }`. The id is the map's name to the server and to saves, and the id of its definition if it has one: 1 to 64 plain characters with no space. A height is `minY + value * stepY` metres, so 16 bits at 1/256 m reach 256 m above `minY`. Without `seaLevel` the map has no water |
| `heights.png` | 16-bit greyscale, a pixel a sample. Or `heights.u16`: the same values in the same order, little-endian, with no header |
| `tint.png` | 8-bit, greyscale or indexed, a pixel a sample: its palette index (`shared/pack/palette.ts`). Or `tint.u8`. Without either, index 0 everywhere |
| `statics.json` | `[{ "kind": "core:wall", "x": 240.5, "y": 1.8, "z": 270, "yaw": 90 }]`. Pieces set down with the world and owned by nobody, by content id and centre. They snap to 1/512 m. Optional |
| `nodes.json` | Layers of resource nodes, described below. Optional |
| `spawns.json` | `[{ "name": "Plaza", "x": 256, "z": 240, "yaw": 0 }]`. 1 to 16. The first is where a new survivor arrives, and a dead one chooses among them |

A PNG must be one channel and not interlaced. `unpack` writes `tint.png` indexed
with the game's palette, so it shows in its colours.

# Shared world layers

Base PNGs without the `_fine` suffix are 4,065 × 4,065 **vertex samples**, with north at row 0. The inclusive endpoints span exactly 8,128 m: sample `(column,row)` is `(−4064 + 2×column, 4064 − 2×row)` metres in the local Transverse Mercator CRS in `../map.json`. There are 4,064 two-metre cells, 127 chunks of 64 m. Read grayscale values as numbers, with no color management or gamma conversion. The PNGs contain no georeferencing tags; `map.json` and this file are authoritative.

The game tile images instead use pixel areas: at zoom z, pixel centers are `(−4064 +(column+.5)×8128/(1024×2^z), 4064−(row+.5)×8128/(1024×2^z))`. This distinction prevents a half-pixel drift.

For the game's 0–100 map overlay, use eastward coordinate `100×(x+4064)/8128` and southward coordinate `100×(4064−y)/8128`. These are normalized game coordinates, not geographic longitude/latitude in degrees. Overlay rendering belongs to the game; it is absent from every tile.

| File | Encoding |
|---|---|
| height.png | Unsigned 16-bit. Height in metres NAVD88 = value/100 − 100. NOAA heights converted from US survey feet with 1200/3937. Bilinear reprojection; 1 cm quantization. |
| height_valid.png | 8-bit: 255 surveyed DEM coverage; 0 absent. Missing heights use −1 m in height.png. **This is an explicit engine convention, not measured bathymetry.** |
| water.png | 8-bit: 1 TIGER water polygon; 0 land. Water beneath elevated bridges is retained. |
| roads.png | 8-bit: 0 none; 1 local/service/path; 2 arterial/highway; 3 road over source water; 4 subterranean tunnel (not painted as a surface bridge); 5 authored missing bridge span. TIGER centerlines are measured geometry; corridor widths are authored: 22 m highway, 14 m arterial, 8 m local, 3–7 m paths/ramps/service. |
| buildings.png | 8-bit: 1 footprint; 0 outside. FEMA/ORNL USA Structures. Includes actual courtyards/holes where supplied. |
| landcover.png | 8-bit NLCD 2021 codes, nearest sampling. 11 water; 21 developed open; 22 low-intensity development; 23 medium; 24 high; 31 barren; 41 deciduous forest; 42 evergreen; 43 mixed; 52 shrub; 71 grass; 81 pasture; 82 crops; 90 woody wetland; 95 emergent wetland; 255 source nodata. Native source is ~30 m, not 2 m. |
| biome.png | Authored succession: 1 water; 2 open urban land; 3 reclaimed vegetation; 4 coastal mangrove; 5 low wetland; 6 sand; 7 ruin footprint; 8 road; 9 bridge. Derived from NLCD, DEM, shore distance and exact geometry. These are fictional future conditions, not surveyed present vegetation. |
| flooded_streets.png | Authored standing water: 1 low street pool; 0 other. Road land below 0.55 m NAVD88, within 300 m of the surveyed coast, excluding buildings; small artifacts removed. Coast geometry is unchanged. |
| bridge_gaps.png | Authored missing spans: 1 gap region; 0 other. Intersect with road-over-water to remove the deck. Four precise vector polygons are in future_changes.geojson. |
| wrecks.png | Authored submerged hulls: 1 footprint; 0 other. Four original fictional objects, not recorded real wreck sites. Positions and outlines in future_changes.geojson; the water above them remains water. |
| painted_canopy.png | 8-bit: 1 added future-world vegetation crown; 0 other. Authored from the registered finest-scale original paintings, excluding water, roads, buildings and beach. Union with biome vegetation classes 3–5 for world placement. Not a tree survey and does not encode heights. |

Four files use a finer grid: `water_fine.png`, `buildings_fine.png`, `roads_fine.png`, and `painted_canopy_fine.png` are 8,192 × 8,192 pixel areas across the same bounds. They use the same respective class encodings. **Use these canonical fine masks or the vectors for world feature placement:** very thin source features can disappear between 2 m samples. The fine geographic masks match the finest painting geometry exactly. The 4,065-sample layers are convenient engine-grid companions, not a lossless substitute for the fine outlines.

The fine canopy preserves close-scale crown outlines; every painted zoom samples this same frozen layer. `painted_canopy.json` records provenance and counts. At the inclusive grid's four outer sample lines, classifications use the adjacent finest pixel inside the square, avoiding a false empty fringe caused by half-open polygon rasterization. `checks/canonical_layers.json` records endpoint corrections. Road tunnels occupy class 4 only where there is no visible surface road; an intersecting surface road retains its surface class.

`areawater.geojson`, `roads.geojson` and `buildings.geojson` retain clipped vector geometry in the **local projected CRS**, not RFC 7946 geographic degrees. Their `crs` member declares it. Use them to render reference images afresh at every zoom. Do not enlarge the 2 m masks for close-scale shoreline tracing.

Known source limits: TIGER is cartographic rather than a modern cadastral coastline survey; FEMA excludes many structures below 450 square feet and does not certify sub-metre positional accuracy. A 1 px painting-registration score measures agreement with these inputs, not their accuracy on Earth. Source dates differ. No ocean bathymetry has been acquired.

"""Register generated pigment, then constrain every visible feature to world geometry."""
import argparse,json,hashlib,inspect
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image,ImageDraw
from scipy import ndimage as nd
from common import *
from reference import grid_at
from alignment import feature_align,shore_align

def load(path,size=None):
    im=Image.open(path).convert('RGB')
    if size:im=im.resize(size,Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
    return np.asarray(im,dtype=np.float32)

def water_rgb(a):return (a[...,1]-a[...,0]>3)&(a[...,2]-a[...,0]>-18)

def sample(a,y,x):
    if a.ndim==2:return nd.map_coordinates(a,[y,x],order=1,mode='nearest')
    return np.stack([nd.map_coordinates(a[...,i],[y,x],order=1,mode='nearest') for i in range(3)],-1)

def register(a,truth,reference=None):
    """Small smooth shoreline correction; final geometry is imposed separately."""
    aligned=False
    register.last_info={}
    if reference is not None:
        a,aligned,info=feature_align(a,reference)
        register.last_info['feature_fit']=info
        print('features',info,flush=True)
    if not aligned and .002<truth.mean()<.998:
        a,info=shore_align(a,truth)
        register.last_info['shore_similarity']=info
        print('shore similarity',info,flush=True)
        aligned=True
    if not aligned and a.shape[0]==1152:
        # Measured fallback for this image tool's expanded framing. Broad water
        # scenes lack unique corners; allow only small shoreline refinements.
        y,x=np.mgrid[:1152,:1152].astype(np.float32)
        a=sample(a,y/1.082,x/1.082)
    wet=water_rgb(a)
    ss=nd.gaussian_filter(nd.distance_transform_edt(wet)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~wet),1)
    ts=nd.gaussian_filter(nd.distance_transform_edt(truth)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~truth),1)
    sy,sx=np.gradient(ss)
    yy,xx=np.mgrid[:truth.shape[0],:truth.shape[1]].astype(np.float32)
    ux=np.zeros_like(xx);uy=np.zeros_like(yy)
    band=np.exp(-(np.abs(ts)/24)**4)
    for _ in range(12):
        delta=ts-sample(ss,yy+uy,xx+ux)
        gy=sample(sy,yy+uy,xx+ux);gx=sample(sx,yy+uy,xx+ux)
        den=gx*gx+gy*gy+(delta/2)**2+1e-4
        ux=nd.gaussian_filter(ux+nd.gaussian_filter(delta*gx/den,1)*band,.65)
        uy=nd.gaussian_filter(uy+nd.gaussian_filter(delta*gy/den,1)*band,.65)
        ux=np.clip(ux,-4,4);uy=np.clip(uy,-4,4)
    a=sample(a,yy+uy,xx+ux)
    # Repair only water, using open-water pigment clear of any inked land.
    # Keep land's original brushwork intact; semantic palettes handle invented
    # inland pools later without nearest-neighbor patchwork across tree crowns.
    wet=water_rgb(a)
    safe=nd.binary_erosion(wet,iterations=10,border_value=1)
    if safe.any():
        inds=nd.distance_transform_edt(~safe,return_distances=False,return_indices=True)
        bad=truth&~safe
        a[bad]=a[inds[0][bad],inds[1][bad]]
        smooth=nd.gaussian_filter(a,(1.6,1.6,0))
        blend=nd.gaussian_filter(bad.astype(np.float32),1.6)*truth
        a=a*(1-blend[...,None])+smooth*blend[...,None]
    return a

def cached_register(path,reference_path,truth,size):
    cache=path.with_name(path.name.replace('.raw.png','.registered.png'))
    meta=cache.with_suffix('.json')
    fingerprint=hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()+reference_path.read_bytes()+truth.tobytes()+
          inspect.getsource(register).encode()+inspect.getsource(feature_align).encode()+inspect.getsource(shore_align).encode()).hexdigest()
    if cache.exists() and meta.exists() and json.loads(meta.read_text()).get('fingerprint')==fingerprint:
        return load(cache)
    a=register(load(path,(size,size)),truth,load(reference_path))
    save(np.uint8(np.clip(a,0,255)),cache)
    meta.write_text(json.dumps({'fingerprint':fingerprint,'raw':path.name,**register.last_info},indent=2))
    return load(cache)

def assemble(z,partial=False):
    n=1024*2**z;count=2**z; ref=ROOT/'references'/f'z{z}'
    truth=np.array(Image.open(ref/'surface_water.png'))>0
    if z==0:return cached_register(ROOT/'paintings/z0/0_0.raw.png',ref/'whole.png',truth,n)
    # Overlapping native-scale paintings; smooth partition of unity in the gutters.
    out=np.zeros((n,n,3),np.float32);total=np.zeros((n,n),np.float32)
    g=64;size=1024+2*g
    ramp=np.ones(size,np.float32);ramp[:2*g]=np.sin(np.linspace(0,np.pi/2,2*g))**2
    ramp[-2*g:]=ramp[:2*g][::-1]
    weight=ramp[:,None]*ramp[None,:]
    padded=np.pad(truth,g,mode='edge')
    for y in range(count):
        for x in range(count):
            p=ROOT/'paintings'/f'z{z}'/f'{x}_{y}.raw.png'
            if not p.exists():
                if not partial:raise FileNotFoundError(p)
                continue
            target=padded[y*1024:y*1024+size,x*1024:x*1024+size]
            a=cached_register(p,ref/f'{x}_{y}.context.png',target,size)
            xa=max(0,x*1024-g);xb=min(n,(x+1)*1024+g)
            ya=max(0,y*1024-g);yb=min(n,(y+1)*1024+g)
            u=xa-(x*1024-g);v=ya-(y*1024-g)
            w=weight[v:v+yb-ya,u:u+xb-xa].copy()
            if x==0:w[:,:g]=ramp[v:v+yb-ya,None]
            if y==0:w[:g,:]=ramp[None,u:u+xb-xa]
            if x==count-1:w[:,-g:]=ramp[v:v+yb-ya,None]
            if y==count-1:w[-g:,:]=ramp[None,u:u+xb-xa]
            if x==0 and y==0:w[:g,:g]=1
            if x==count-1 and y==0:w[:g,-g:]=1
            if x==0 and y==count-1:w[-g:,:g]=1
            if x==count-1 and y==count-1:w[-g:,-g:]=1
            out[ya:yb,xa:xb]+=a[v:v+yb-ya,u:u+xb-xa]*w[...,None]
            total[ya:yb,xa:xb]+=w
    out/=np.maximum(total[...,None],1e-6)
    if partial:
        parent_path=ROOT/'paintings'/f'z{z-1}'/'final-master.png'
        if not parent_path.exists():parent_path=ROOT/'checks'/f'partial_z{z-1}.png'
        parent=load(parent_path,(n,n));missing=total<.999
        out[missing]=out[missing]*total[missing,None]+parent[missing]*(1-total[missing,None])
    return out

def pigment(lum,rg,gb):
    # Distinct physical pigment families make geometry measurable directly in RGB.
    g=np.clip(lum,gb+2,253-rg)
    return np.stack([g+rg,g,g-gb],-1)

def finish(z,partial=False):
    n=1024*2**z;mpp=SIZE/n; ref=ROOT/'references'/f'z{z}'
    raw=assemble(z,partial)
    save(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),ROOT/'paintings'/f'z{z}'/'registered.png')
    w=np.array(Image.open(ref/'surface_water.png'))>0
    rd=np.array(Image.open(ref/'roads.png'))>0
    b=np.array(Image.open(ref/'buildings.png'))>0
    bio=np.array(Image.open(ref/'biome.png'))
    # Remove invented architectural boundaries, retain gently varying wash.
    l=raw.mean(2);soft=nd.gaussian_filter(l,2.2+z*.65)
    fine=np.clip(l-nd.gaussian_filter(l,.65),-22,22)

    # invented houses. Crisp detail is reserved for the constrained feature masks.

        crown=nd.binary_closing(crown,iterations=1)

    green=raw.copy();green[...,1]=np.clip(150+(raw[...,1]-150)*.85,70,195)
    green[...,0]=green[...,1]+np.clip(raw[...,0]-raw[...,1],-8,12)
    green[...,2]=green[...,1]-np.clip(raw[...,1]-raw[...,2],46,66)

    beach=bio==6

    yy,xx=np.indices((n,n),dtype=np.int32)

        hatch=((xx+yy*2)%(8+z)==0)&(db>1)&(db<4+z)

      const allow = new Uint8Array(Math.ceil(image.data.length / 8));
      const pixels = image.data.reverse();
      for (let bit = 0; bit < pixels.length; bit++) if (pixels[bit]! >= 128) allow[bit >> 3]! |= 1 << (bit & 7);
      return { ...scatter, allowCell: cell, allow };
    }
    // A node's slot is its place among its chunk's rows, which keep the order they are listed in.
    const rows = layer.list.map((n) => ({ ...n, chunk: chunkAt(dims, n.x, n.z) })).sort((a, b) => a.chunk - b.chunk);
    const kinds = [...new Set(rows.map((n) => n.kind))];
    const first = new Uint32Array(chunkCount(dims) + 1);
    for (const n of rows) first[n.chunk + 1]!++;
    for (let c = 0; c < chunkCount(dims); c++) first[c + 1]! += first[c]!;
    const within = (at: number, corner: number): number => Math.min(65535, Math.max(0, Math.round((at - corner * CHUNK_SIZE) * NODE_UNITS)));
    return {

-For the game's 0–100 map overlay, use eastward coordinate `100×(x+4064)/8128` and southward coordinate `100×(4064−y)/8128`. These are normalized game coordinates, not geographic longitude/latitude in degrees. Overlay rendering belongs to the game; it is absent from every tile.
+For screen coordinates on the north-up picture, use eastward `u = 100×(E+4064)/8128` and southward `v = 100×(4064−N)/8128`, where `(E,N)` are our local projected easting/northing. These are picture coordinates, **not engine x/z** and not geographic longitude/latitude. Overlay rendering belongs to the game; it is absent from every tile.
+
+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

"""Robust global geometry alignment; constrain repeated urban corners by position."""
import cv2 as cv
import numpy as np
from scipy import ndimage as nd
from scipy.optimize import minimize
from PIL import Image

def shore_align(paint,truth):
    """Fit island silhouettes using a similarity transform, without urban shear."""
    n=256
    wet=(paint[...,1]-paint[...,0]>3)&(paint[...,2]-paint[...,0]>-18)
    def clean(a):
        a=np.asarray(Image.fromarray(a).resize((n,n),Image.Resampling.NEAREST))
        a=nd.binary_closing(a,iterations=2,border_value=1)
        labels,count=nd.label(a)
        if count:
            sizes=np.bincount(labels.ravel());sizes[0]=0;a=labels==sizes.argmax()
        return a
    sm=clean(wet);tm=clean(truth)
    sd=nd.distance_transform_edt(sm)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sm)
    td=nd.distance_transform_edt(tm)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~tm)
    yy,xx=np.mgrid[:n,:n].astype(np.float32);xc=xx-n/2;yc=yy-n/2
    weight=.15+np.exp(-(np.abs(td)/18)**2)
    def loss(p):
        scale,angle,dx,dy=p;c=np.cos(angle);s=np.sin(angle)
        v=nd.map_coordinates(sd,[scale*(s*xc+c*yc)+n/2+dy,scale*(c*xc-s*yc)+n/2+dx],order=1,mode='nearest')
        delta=np.clip(v,-32,32)-np.clip(td,-32,32)
        return np.sum(np.sqrt(delta*delta+.25)*weight)/weight.sum()
    starts=[[1,0,0,0],[1/1.082,0,-(1-1/1.082)*128,-(1-1/1.082)*128]]
    fits=[minimize(loss,p,method='Powell',bounds=[(.85,1.15),(-.035,.035),(-24,24),(-24,24)],
                   options={'maxiter':80,'xtol':.0001,'ftol':.00001}) for p in starts]
    fit=min(fits,key=lambda f:f.fun);scale,angle,dx,dy=fit.x;c=np.cos(angle);s=np.sin(angle)
    h,w=truth.shape;yy,xx=np.mgrid[:h,:w].astype(np.float32);xc=xx-w/2;yc=yy-h/2
    sy=scale*(s*xc+c*yc)+h/2+dy*h/256;sx=scale*(c*xc-s*yc)+w/2+dx*w/256
    out=np.stack([nd.map_coordinates(paint[...,i],[sy,sx],order=1,mode='reflect') for i in range(3)],-1)
    return out,{'method':'silhouette_similarity_multistart','parameters':fit.x.tolist(),'loss':float(fit.fun)}

def feature_align(paint,reference):
    cv.setRNGSeed(117)
    gray1=cv.cvtColor(np.uint8(paint),cv.COLOR_RGB2GRAY)
    gray2=cv.cvtColor(np.uint8(reference),cv.COLOR_RGB2GRAY)
    sift=cv.SIFT_create(nfeatures=16000,contrastThreshold=.01)
    k1,d1=sift.detectAndCompute(gray1,None);k2,d2=sift.detectAndCompute(gray2,None)
    if d1 is None or d2 is None:return paint,False,{'method':'no_features'}
    pairs=cv.BFMatcher().knnMatch(d1,d2,k=2)
    good=[m for pair in pairs if len(pair)==2 for m,n in [pair] if m.distance<.85*n.distance]
    if len(good)<6:return paint,False,{'method':'too_few_matches','matches':len(good)}
    a=np.float32([k1[m.queryIdx].pt for m in good]);b=np.float32([k2[m.trainIdx].pt for m in good])
    best=None
    for scale in [1.0,1.082]:
        local=np.linalg.norm(a*scale-b,axis=1)<48
        if local.sum()<6:continue
        mat,inside=cv.estimateAffinePartial2D(a[local],b[local],method=cv.RANSAC,
              ransacReprojThreshold=5,maxIters=10000,confidence=.999)
        if mat is None or inside is None:continue
        inside=inside.ravel().astype(bool);count=int(inside.sum())
        s=np.hypot(mat[0,0],mat[1,0]);angle=np.degrees(np.arctan2(mat[1,0],mat[0,0]))
        span=np.ptp(b[local][inside],axis=0) if count else [0,0]
        if count<8 or not(.9<s<1.16) or abs(angle)>2 or np.any(np.abs(mat[:,2])>70) or min(span)<100:continue
        if best is None or count>best[0]:best=(count,mat,a[local][inside],b[local][inside])
    if best is None:return paint,False,{'method':'rejected_feature_fit','matches':len(good)}
    count,mat,aa,bb=best
    error=np.linalg.norm(aa@mat[:,:2].T+mat[:,2]-bb,axis=1)
    aligned=cv.warpAffine(paint,mat,(paint.shape[1],paint.shape[0]),flags=cv.INTER_LINEAR,borderMode=cv.BORDER_REFLECT_101)
    return aligned,True,{'method':'SIFT_position_constrained_RANSAC','inliers':count,
              'median_residual_px':float(np.median(error)),'matrix':mat.tolist()}

 The game tile images instead use pixel areas: at zoom z, pixel centers are `(−4064 +(column+.5)×8128/(1024×2^z), 4064−(row+.5)×8128/(1024×2^z))`. This distinction prevents a half-pixel drift.
 
-For the game's 0–100 map overlay, use eastward coordinate `100×(x+4064)/8128` and southward coordinate `100×(4064−y)/8128`. These are normalized game coordinates, not geographic longitude/latitude in degrees. Overlay rendering belongs to the game; it is absent from every tile.
+For screen coordinates on the north-up picture, use eastward `u = 100×(E+4064)/8128` and southward `v = 100×(4064−N)/8128`, where `(E,N)` are our local projected easting/northing. These are picture coordinates, **not engine x/z** and not geographic longitude/latitude. Overlay rendering belongs to the game; it is absent from every tile.
+
+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

/bin/zsh -lc "cat > tools/mapart/round2.py <<'PY'
\"\"\"Scale-aware ink-and-wash finishing. Saved originals are the only paint inputs.

Round two intentionally separates semantic generalization from geographic precision.
Run "'`round2.py finish Z`, then `round2_measure.py`. See README for provenance.
"""
import argparse, json, math
import cv2
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
from scipy import ndimage as nd
from common import ROOT, SIZE, B, vectors, burn, save
from reference import grid_at
from finish import load, assemble, sample
from alignment import shore_align

PAPER=np.array([237,225,198],np.float32)
INK=np.array([80,73,51],np.float32)


def wet(a):
    return (a[...,1]-a[...,0]>3)&(a[...,2]-a[...,0]>-18)


def far_register(a,truth):
    """Silhouette-only fit avoids matching invented landmark windows to real blocks."""
    a,info=shore_align(a,truth)
    # A smooth elastic correction brings island silhouettes into place without
    # applying the old nearest-neighbour coast repair to the entire water field.
    sm=wet(a)
    sm=nd.binary_closing(sm,iterations=2,border_value=1)
    sd=nd.gaussian_filter(nd.distance_transform_edt(sm)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sm),1.2)
    td=nd.gaussian_filter(nd.distance_transform_edt(truth)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~truth),1.2)
    sy,sx=np.gradient(sd)
    yy,xx=np.mgrid[:truth.shape[0],:truth.shape[1]].astype(np.float32)
    ux=np.zeros_like(xx);uy=np.zeros_like(yy)
    for _ in range(75):
        delta=td-sample(sd,yy+uy,xx+ux)
        gx=sample(sx,yy+uy,xx+ux);gy=sample(sy,yy+uy,xx+ux)
        den=gx*gx+gy*gy+(delta/2)**2+1e-4
        band=np.exp(-(np.abs(td)/40)**4)
        ux=nd.gaussian_filter(ux+delta*gx/den*band,1.4)
        uy=nd.gaussian_filter(uy+delta*gy/den*band,1.4)
        ux=np.clip(ux,-16,16);uy=np.clip(uy,-16,16)
    return sample(a,yy+uy,xx+ux),info


def major_roads(z,n):
    water=np.array(Image.open(ROOT/f'"'references/z{z}/water.png'))>0
    chosen=[]
    for g,p in vectors('roads'):
        if 'tunl' in (p['name'] or '').lower():continue
        name=p['name'] or ''
        keep=p['mtfcc'] in ['S1100','S1200'] or any(t in name for t in ['Venetian','Dade Blvd'])
        if z==1: keep=keep or name in ['N Miami Ave','S Miami Ave','Washington Ave','Meridian Ave','West Ave','NE 2nd Ave','NW 2nd Ave']
        if z>=2:keep=True
        if keep:chosen.append((g.buffer(p['width_m']/2,cap_style=2,join_style=2),1))
    rd=burn(chosen,n)>0
    # Preserve every causeway, including local road sections over the bay.
    allrd=np.array(Image.open(ROOT/f'references/z{z}/roads.png'))>0
    rd|=allrd&water
    gaps=burn([(g,1) for g,p in vectors('future_changes') if p['kind']=='missing_bridge_span'],n)>0
    return rd&~gaps


def paper_texture(n):
    # Reuse original rag-paper tooth at every zoom; no new random noise field.
    sheet=load(ROOT/'style/style-sheet.png')
    swatch=sheet[-28:,-210:-10].mean(2)
    swatch=swatch-nd.gaussian_filter(swatch,2)
    return np.tile(swatch,(math.ceil(n/swatch.shape[0]),math.ceil(n/swatch.shape[1])))[:n,:n]*.32


def coasts(out,w,bio,z):
    \"\"\"Subpixel wavering, interrupted ink and doubled quays on a continuous canvas.\"\"\"
    n=len(w);mpp=SIZE/n
    dw=nd.distance_transform_edt(w).astype(np.float32)
    dl=nd.distance_transform_edt(~w).astype(np.float32)
    yy,xx=np.mgrid[:n,:n].astype(np.float32)
    # At most 0.8 pixel hand variation. Same world phase at all scales.
    u=xx/2**z;v=yy/2**z
    wave=.42*np.sin(u*.41+v*.28)+.24*np.sin(u*.93-v*.71)
    signed=dw-dl
    width=.70+.28*np.sin(u*.19+v*.23)+.22*np.sin(u*.69-v*.31)
    coast=np.maximum(0,1-np.abs(signed-wave)/(width+1.1))
    beach=nd.maximum_filter((bio==6).astype(np.float32),size=5)>0
    coast[beach]*=.15
    # Broken pen lift; never removes the true land/water division.
    lift=np.clip((np.sin(u*.31+v*.17)+.35)*1.5,0,1)
    alpha=coast*(.30+.52*lift)
    out=out*(1-alpha[...,None])+INK*alpha[...,None]
    # A second short stroke on the landward side of urban quays.
    quay=(~w)&(bio"'!=6)&~np.isin(bio,[3,4,5])
    double=np.exp(-((dl-2.2)/.5)**2)*quay*(np.sin(u*.17-v*.29)>.25)*.24
    out=out*(1-double[...,None])+INK*double[...,None]
    # Contour-following pale wash: land geometry controls every shallow.
    shall=np.exp(-dw/max(2.4,27/mpp))*w*.23
    out=out*(1-shall[...,None])+np.array([176,197,174])*shall[...,None]
    return out


def story(im,z,rd):
    """Only saved world objects: missing spans and wrecks, at exact locations."""
    n=im.width;mpp=SIZE/n;d=ImageDraw.Draw(im)
    def px(p):return ((p[0]-B[0])/mpp,(B[3]-p[1])/mpp)
    for g,p in vectors('"'future_changes'):
        if p['kind']=='submerged_wreck':
            pts=[px(t) for t in g.exterior.coords]
            d.line(pts,fill=(74,103,89),width=1)
            angle=math.radians(p['angle_degrees']);dx=math.cos(angle);dy=math.sin(angle)
            cx,cy=p['center'];length=p['length_m'];width=p['width_m']
            for u in np.arange(-length*.36,length*.35,max(5,mpp*1.6)):
                d.line([px((cx+u*dx-v*dy,cy+u*dy+v*dx)) for v in [-width*.45,width*.45]],fill=(77,102,84),width=1)
        elif p['kind']=='missing_bridge_span':
            # End-cap rubble remains inside existing surviving road pixels.
            gm=burn([(g.buffer(mpp*1.5),1)],n)>0
            arr=np.array(im);rim=gm&rd
            arr[rim]=arr[rim]*.48+INK*.52
            im=Image.fromarray(arr);d=ImageDraw.Draw(im)
    return im


def finish(z):
    n=1024*2**z;mpp=SIZE/n;ref=ROOT/f'references/z{z}'
    w=np.array(Image.open(ref/'surface_water.png'))>0
    b=np.array(Image.open(ref/'buildings.png'))>0
    bio=np.array(Image.open(ref/'biome.png'))
    rd=major_roads(z,n)
    if z==0:
        raw,info=far_register(load(ROOT/'paintings/z0/0_0.raw.png',(n,n)),w)
        (ROOT/'paintings/z0/0_0.registered.json').write_text(json.dumps(info,indent=2))
    elif z==1:
        raw=assemble(z)
    else:raw=assemble(z)
    save(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),ROOT/f'paintings/z{z}/registered.png')
    lum=raw.mean(2);fine=lum-nd.gaussian_filter(lum,.8)
    tooth=paper_texture(n)
    if z<=1:
        out=raw.copy()
        # Fill wrongly painted water outside coast with paper only at coastline.
        dl=nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
        repair=(~w)&wet(raw)&(dl<9)&~rd
        out[repair]=PAPER+fine[repair,None]*.55
    else:
        # Preserve the independently painted masonry, trees and courtyards.
        # Exposed substrate is now ivory with original rag tooth, not opaque tan.
        broad=nd.gaussian_filter(lum,16)
        out=PAPER[None,None,:]+((broad-195)*.12+tooth)[...,None]
        nature=np.isin(bio,[3,4,5])
        canopy=np.array(Image.open(ROOT/'base/painted_canopy_fine.png').resize((n,n),Image.Resampling.NEAREST))>0
        nature=(nature|canopy)&~(w|b|rd)
        out[nature]=raw[nature]*.83+np.array([191,193,144])*.17
        # Sparse original drybrush in the paper, rather than all generated roads.
        dry=~(w|b|rd|nature)
        detail=np.clip(fine,-18,12)*.35
        out[dry]+=detail[dry,None]
        beach=(bio==6)&dry
        out[beach]=np.array([238,222,182])+fine[beach,None]*.55+tooth[beach,None]
        masonry=raw.copy()
        # Remove hue errors while allowing warm-grey walls, pale lime and ink.
        ml=masonry.mean(2)
        masonry=np.stack([ml+10,ml+4,ml-12],-1)
        db=nd.distance_transform_edt(b)
        edge=b&(db<=1)
        masonry[edge]=masonry[edge]*.44+INK*.56
        out[b]=masonry[b]
        # Distinct district treatment, anchored in world coordinates.
        yy,xx=np.mgrid[:n,:n].astype(np.float32);u=xx/n;v=yy/n
        port=(u>.29)&(u<.77)&(v>.49)&(v<.70)&b
        beachhotel=(u>.87)&(v>.28)&(v<.73)&b
        downtown=(u>.13)&(u<.28)&(v>.4)&(v<.79)&b
        out[port]=out[port]*.9+np.array([157,117,74])*.1
        out[beachhotel]=out[beachhotel]*.82+np.array([237,225,199])*.18
        out[downtown]*=.91
    # Paint continuous water from generated pigment, avoiding nearest-fill streaks.
    safe=wet(raw)&w
    sig=max(8,40/mpp);den=nd.gaussian_filter(safe.astype(np.float32),sig)
    water=raw.copy()
    for k in range(3):
        field=nd.gaussian_filter(raw[...,k]*safe,sig)/np.maximum(den,1e-5)
        field=np.where(den>.02,field,[113,153,143][k])
        bad=~safe
        water[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
    # Retain water tooth/current marks but suppress invented submerged objects.
    water=water*.86+np.array([146,174,158])*.14
    out[w]=water[w]
    # Major avenues only in far views; all native road corridors in close views.
    dr=nd.distance_transform_edt(rd)
    rpaint=np.array([235,222,190])+fine[...,None]*.30+tooth[...,None]
    edge=rd&(dr<=1)
    rpaint[edge]=rpaint[edge]*.85+INK*.15
    out[rd]=rpaint[rd]
    flood=(grid_at('flooded_streets',n)>0)&~b
    # Flood remains the same world layer at every scale, with darker ink banks.
    out[flood]=np.array([123,159,144])+fine[flood,None]*.35
    out=coasts(out,w,bio,z)
    if z>0:
        # Full RGB broad pigment agreement, separated by coast to avoid halos.
        parent=load(ROOT/f'paintings/z{z-1}/final-master.png',(n,n))
        for mask in [w,~w]:
            mf=mask.astype(np.float32);sig=12;den=nd.gaussian_filter(mf,sig)
            for k in range(3):
                a=nd.gaussian_filter(out[...,k]*mf,sig)/np.maximum(den,.001)
                p=nd.gaussian_filter(parent[...,k]*mf,sig)/np.maximum(den,.001)
                delta=np.clip(p-a,-100,100)*.98
                out[...,k][mask]+=delta[mask]
    out=np.uint8(np.clip(out,0,255))
    im=story(Image.fromarray(out),z,rd)
    im.save(ROOT/f'paintings/z{z}/final-master.png')
    dest=ROOT/f'tiles/z{z}';dest.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    for y in range(2**z):
        for x in range(2**z):im.crop((x*1024,y*1024,(x+1)*1024,(y+1)*1024)).save(dest/f'{x}_{y}.png')
    im.resize((1024,1024),Image.Resampling.LANCZOS).save(ROOT/f'checks/overview_z{z}.png')
    save(rd.astype('uint8'),ref/'drawn_roads.png')
    print('round-two finish',z,flush=True)


if __name__=='__main__':
    p=argparse.ArgumentParser();p.add_argument('command',choices=['finish']);p.add_argument('zoom',type=int);a=p.parse_args()
    finish(a.zoom)

+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

 The game tile images instead use pixel areas: at zoom z, pixel centers are `(−4064 +(column+.5)×8128/(1024×2^z), 4064−(row+.5)×8128/(1024×2^z))`. This distinction prevents a half-pixel drift.
 
-For the game's 0–100 map overlay, use eastward coordinate `100×(x+4064)/8128` and southward coordinate `100×(4064−y)/8128`. These are normalized game coordinates, not geographic longitude/latitude in degrees. Overlay rendering belongs to the game; it is absent from every tile.
+For screen coordinates on the north-up picture, use eastward `u = 100×(E+4064)/8128` and southward `v = 100×(4064−N)/8128`, where `(E,N)` are our local projected easting/northing. These are picture coordinates, **not engine x/z** and not geographic longitude/latitude. Overlay rendering belongs to the game; it is absent from every tile.
+
+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

 The game tile images instead use pixel areas: at zoom z, pixel centers are `(−4064 +(column+.5)×8128/(1024×2^z), 4064−(row+.5)×8128/(1024×2^z))`. This distinction prevents a half-pixel drift.
 
-For the game's 0–100 map overlay, use eastward coordinate `100×(x+4064)/8128` and southward coordinate `100×(4064−y)/8128`. These are normalized game coordinates, not geographic longitude/latitude in degrees. Overlay rendering belongs to the game; it is absent from every tile.
+For screen coordinates on the north-up picture, use eastward `u = 100×(E+4064)/8128` and southward `v = 100×(4064−N)/8128`, where `(E,N)` are our local projected easting/northing. These are picture coordinates, **not engine x/z** and not geographic longitude/latitude. Overlay rendering belongs to the game; it is absent from every tile.
+
+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def district_ink(out,z):
+    """Data-clipped structural drawing: port trusses and beach-hotel galleries."""
+    if z<2:return out
+    from shapely.geometry import Polygon,LineString
+    n=len(out);mpp=SIZE/n

+    im=Image.fromarray(np.uint8(np.clip(out,0,255)));d=ImageDraw.Draw(im)

+            parts=list(line.geoms) if hasattr(line,'geoms') else [line]

+                pts=[((x-B[0])/mpp,(B[3]-y)/mpp) for x,y in part.coords]
+                d.line(pts,fill=(125,99,67) if isport else (143,132,105),width=1)
+    return np.asarray(im,dtype=np.float32)

+For screen coordinates on the north-up picture, use eastward `u = 100×(E+4064)/8128` and southward `v = 100×(4064−N)/8128`, where `(E,N)` are our local projected easting/northing. +## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+        if length<25 or width<8:continue
+        inner=geom.buffer(-1.5)

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

 The game tile images instead use pixel areas: at zoom z, pixel centers are `(−4064 +(column+.5)×8128/(1024×2^z), 4064−(row+.5)×8128/(1024×2^z))`. This distinction prevents a half-pixel drift.

+For screen coordinates on the north-up picture, use eastward `u = 100×(E+4064)/8128` and southward `v = 100×(4064−N)/8128`, where `(E,N)` are our local projected easting/northing. +
+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

 The game tile images instead use pixel areas: at zoom z, pixel centers are `(−4064 +(column+.5)×8128/(1024×2^z), 4064−(row+.5)×8128/(1024×2^z))`. This distinction prevents a half-pixel drift.

+For screen coordinates on the north-up picture, use eastward `u = 100×(E+4064)/8128` and southward `v = 100×(4064−N)/8128`, where `(E,N)` are our local projected easting/northing. These are picture coordinates, **not engine x/z** and not geographic longitude/latitude. Overlay rendering belongs to the game; it is absent from every tile.
+
+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
 
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
 
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+For screen coordinates on the north-up picture, use eastward `u = 100×(E+4064)/8128` and southward `v = 100×(4064−N)/8128`, where `(E,N)` are our local projected easting/northing. These are picture coordinates, **not engine x/z** and not geographic longitude/latitude. Overlay rendering belongs to the game; it is absent from every tile.
+
+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
 
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw
