+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+## Round two: scale and paper take priority
+
+The first finish lost the paper and forced all 11,919 footprints into every scale. The new overview and district originals use the same original style sheet with these stronger decisions:
+
+- **z0:** main avenues/causeways only; districts described by ivory intervals, loose wash and directional hatching. +- **z2/z3:** the actual footprint fabric returns. Keep independently painted roofless rooms and vegetation; differentiate warehouse trusses, pale beach galleries, darker downtown masonry and low residential shells.
+- **Substrate:** exposed ivory, approximately #EDE1C6, with original rag tooth. The earlier land-wash anchor is a transparent pigment, never an opaque fill across all land. Quiet teal water may show paper tooth too.
+- **Coast:** a geographically constrained hand, with variable pressure, short pen lifts, doubled quay strokes, almost no outline across a beach, and coast-following jade shallows. Do not encode all materials into rigid RGB categories merely to obtain perfect colour-classification scores.
+- **Narrative:** actual saved missing spans and flooded streets stay in the rendering. Symbols communicate the drowned district at far scales; exact corridors and open rooms take over close up. Never add cranes to residential islands or invented wrecks to empty water.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.
+

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)

+    for k in range(3):

+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

"""Verify delivery structure and emit SHA-256 inventory without modifying sources."""
import hashlib,json,struct
from datetime import datetime,timezone
from PIL import Image
import numpy as np
from common import ROOT,CFG,N

def png_info(p):
    with p.open('rb') as f:header=f.read(29)
    assert header[:8]==b'\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n',p
    w,h,depth,color=struct.unpack('>IIBB',header[16:26])
    return {'width':w,'height':h,'bit_depth':depth,'color_type':color}

def main():
    assert CFG['size_m']==8128 and N==4065
    assert (N-1)*2==127*64
    result={'time_utc':datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),'layers':{},'zooms':{},'files':{}}
    for p in sorted((ROOT/'base').glob('*.png')):
        info=png_info(p);fine=p.name.endswith('_fine.png')
        assert info['width']==info['height']==(8192 if fine else N),(p,info)
        assert info['bit_depth']==(16 if p.name=='height.png' else 8),(p,info)
        assert info['color_type']==0,(p,info)
        a=np.asarray(Image.open(p));info['minimum']=int(a.min());info['maximum']=int(a.max())
        if p.name!='height.png':info['value_counts']={str(v):int(c) for v,c in zip(*np.unique(a,return_counts=True))}
        result['layers'][p.name]=info
    for z in range(4):
        count=2**z
        expected={f'{x}_{y}.png' for y in range(count) for x in range(count)}
        found={p.name for p in (ROOT/'tiles'/f'z{z}').glob('*.png')}
        assert expected==found,(z,'missing',expected-found,'extra',found-expected)
        for y in range(count):
            for x in range(count):
                p=ROOT/'tiles'/f'z{z}'/f'{x}_{y}.png';info=png_info(p)
                assert info=={'width':1024,'height':1024,'bit_depth':8,'color_type':2},(p,info)
                assert (ROOT/'paintings'/f'z{z}'/f'{x}_{y}.raw.png').exists()
                assert (ROOT/'paintings'/f'z{z}'/f'{x}_{y}.prompt.txt').exists()
        result['zooms'][str(z)]={'tile_count':count*count,'m_per_pixel':8128/(1024*count),'all_originals_present':True}
    # Hash all delivery layers, vector inputs, style, prompts, original/final paint
    # and references. Raw downloads have their separate frozen manifest.
    for folder in ['base','tiles','style','paintings','references']:
        for p in sorted((ROOT/folder).rglob('*')):
            if p.is_file():result['files'][str(p.relative_to(ROOT))]={'bytes':p.stat().st_size,'sha256':hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()}
    dest=ROOT/'checks/delivery_audit.json';dest.write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2))
    print('PASS: 85 RGB tiles, 85 originals, base grid and bit depth,',len(result['files']),'hashed artifacts')

if __name__=='__main__':main()

+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.

+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.

+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.
+

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

\"\"\"Share broad-pigment differences between four independent continuous paintings.

No geometric resampling of final ink. Reductions are only used to estimate RGB
wash corrections; each native painting keeps its own high-frequency drawing.
\"\"\"
import json
import cv2
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from scipy import ndimage as nd
from common import ROOT


def scores(images):
    return [float(np.abs(nd.gaussian_filter(cv2.resize(images[z+1],(len(images[z]),)*2,interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)-images[z],(8,8,0))).mean()) for z in range(3)]


def main():
    images=[np.array(Image.open(ROOT/f'paintings/z{z}/unbalanced-master.png'),np.float32) for z in range(4)]
    log={'method':'symmetric continuous-canvas broad RGB wash relaxation, sigma 8 at each parent scale; native marks stay in place','initial':scores(images),'passes':[]}
    print('initial',log['initial'],flush=True)
    for step in range(14):
        # Alternate traversal prevents the last pair from dominating the chain.
        for z in ([2,1,0] if step%2==0 else [0,1,2]):
            parent=images[z];child=images[z+1];n=len(parent)
            small=cv2.resize(child,(n,n),interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
            field=nd.gaussian_filter(small-parent,(8,8,0))
            field=np.clip(field,-12,12)
            parent+=field*.48
            # Chunking channel updates avoids a second full RGB 8k allocation.
            for k in range(3):
                big=cv2.resize(field[...,k],(n*2,n*2),interpolation=cv2.INTER_LINEAR)
                child[...,k]-=big*.52
            np.clip(parent,0,255,out=parent);np.clip(child,0,255,out=child)
        err=scores(images);log['passes'].append(err);print('pass',step+1,err,flush=True)
        if max(err)<1.65:break
    for z,a in enumerate(images):
        im=Image.fromarray(np.uint8(np.clip(np.rint(a),0,255)))
        im.save(ROOT/f'paintings/z{z}/final-master.png')
        for y in range(2**z):
            for x in range(2**z):im.crop((x*1024,y*1024,(x+1)*1024,(y+1)*1024)).save(ROOT/f'tiles/z{z}/{x}_{y}.png')
        im.resize((1024,1024),Image.Resampling.LANCZOS).save(ROOT/f'checks/overview_z{z}.png')
    log['final_float']=scores(images)
    (ROOT/'reports/round2-balance.json').write_text(json.dumps(log,indent=2))

if __name__=='__main__':main()

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)

+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+## Round two: scale and paper take priority
+
+The first finish lost the paper and forced all 11,919 footprints into every scale. The new overview and district originals use the same original style sheet with these stronger decisions:
+
+- **z0:** main avenues/causeways only; districts described by ivory intervals, loose wash and directional hatching. +- **z1:** spaced source-building anchors and groups of ruins, more canals and park detail, still generous unpainted ground. Do not bring back the complete minor-road or house mesh.
+- **z2/z3:** the actual footprint fabric returns. Keep independently painted roofless rooms and vegetation; differentiate warehouse trusses, pale beach galleries, darker downtown masonry and low residential shells.
+- **Substrate:** exposed ivory, approximately #EDE1C6, with original rag tooth. The earlier land-wash anchor is a transparent pigment, never an opaque fill across all land. Quiet teal water may show paper tooth too.
+- **Coast:** a geographically constrained hand, with variable pressure, short pen lifts, doubled quay strokes, almost no outline across a beach, and coast-following jade shallows. Do not encode all materials into rigid RGB categories merely to obtain perfect colour-classification scores.
+- **Narrative:** actual saved missing spans and flooded streets stay in the rendering. Symbols communicate the drowned district at far scales; exact corridors and open rooms take over close up. Never add cranes to residential islands or invented wrecks to empty water.
+

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.
+

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.
+

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw
