+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.
+

 | height.png | Unsigned 16-bit. Height in metres NAVD88 = value/100 − 100. NOAA heights converted from US survey feet with 1200/3937. Bilinear reprojection; 1 cm quantization. |

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.
+

Do not use the old `finish.py` entry point to export the round-two delivery: its all-features-at-all-scales treatment is the artistic behavior replaced in this round. Its registration/overlap helpers are still used for the close original paintings.
+
+Saved originals are sufficient to reproduce the current artwork; no image calls or downloads are needed when the base vectors and PNGs are present:
+
+```sh
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/reference.py
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 0
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 1
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 2
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 3
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2_balance.py
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2_measure.py
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/audit.py
+```
+
+Close-tile registration additionally needs the native 64-pixel geometry contexts. If `references/` was removed, run `round2_close_contexts.py` for z2 and the original `contexts.py 3` after a parent master exists. For z3, existing queue entries can prevent context regeneration; `round2_restore.py` reconstructs the geometry contexts without altering the historical used prompts and is the preferred clean-checkout path (run it immediately after `reference.py`). Contexts used for registration contain geometry, not the parent painting, so the generation-time parent is not needed to re-finish saved originals.
+
+| Round-two tool | Purpose |
+|---|---|
+| round2.py generalized 0 | Rebuild the overview's generalized plan from native vectors and spaced footprint anchors. The exact generation-time reference is also preserved as paintings/z0/geometry-input.png. |
+| round2.py contexts 1 | Prepare four generalized district references, parent crops and prompts for **new** image generation. Overwrites the z1 queue/prompts; not necessary for reproduction. |
+| round2_close_contexts.py | Prepare sixteen native neighborhood references and new district-parent crops; writes round2-queue.json. The accepted outputs replace z2 originals in place. |
+| round2.py finish Z | Continuous native canvas, scale-selected roads, geography-constrained coast, exposed rag paper, data-clipped architecture and district treatments. Keeps z3's original room paintings. Writes an ignored unbalanced-master.png and provisional final-master/tiles. |
+| round2_balance.py | Share broad RGB wash corrections across all four independent paintings without moving any ink geometry; cut final 1,024² tiles only after the continuous-canvas adjustment. |
+| round2_measure.py | All 140 separate tile joins, zero-loss reconstruction, adjacent-zoom RGB/8-pixel broad comparison, explicit limited pigment-boundary diagnostic, selected road support, and retained SHA-256 inventory. |
+| round2_restore.py | Recreate native registration contexts and review sheets from kept layers/originals/tiles. |
+
+Measurements, production notes and delivery audit are retained under `assets/source/maps/miami/reports/`, and interpreted in `REPORT.md`. `checks/` contains only regenerable review pictures, external comparison copies, and experiments. Raw downloads, references, warped copies and continuous finishing masters are ignored. No runtime/engine package or map file is produced.
+
+The built-in image tool was used for every new raster painting. Exact prompts are beside the originals. The corrected z1 northeast original also has a correction prompt and its preceding source under `paintings/z1/studies/`. The first new overview study is retained under `style/` because it supplied art direction to the accepted overview. Foreign comparison images were inspected only, never passed to image generation. Generation itself is nondeterministic; the saved originals make finishing reproducible.

+def assemble_far(z,w):
+    n=len(w);g=64;s=1152
+    out=np.zeros((n,n,3),np.float32);total=np.zeros((n,n),np.float32)
+    ramp=np.ones(s,np.float32);ramp[:128]=np.sin(np.linspace(0,np.pi/2,128))**2;ramp[-128:]=ramp[:128][::-1]
+    weight=ramp[:,None]*ramp[None,:];padded=np.pad(w,g,mode='edge')
+    for y in range(2**z):
+        for x in range(2**z):
+            p=ROOT/f'paintings/z{z}/{x}_{y}.raw.png'
+            a,info=far_register(load(p,(s,s)),padded[y*1024:y*1024+s,x*1024:x*1024+s])
+            p.with_name(f'{x}_{y}.registered.json').write_text(json.dumps(info,indent=2))
+            xa=max(0,x*1024-g);xb=min(n,(x+1)*1024+g);ya=max(0,y*1024-g);yb=min(n,(y+1)*1024+g)
+            u=xa-(x*1024-g);v=ya-(y*1024-g);q=weight[v:v+yb-ya,u:u+xb-xa]
+            out[ya:yb,xa:xb]+=a[v:v+yb-ya,u:u+xb-xa]*q[...,None];total[ya:yb,xa:xb]+=q
+    return out/np.maximum(total[...,None],1e-6)

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.
+

+- **Coast:** a geographically constrained hand, with variable pressure, short pen lifts, doubled quay strokes, almost no outline across a beach, and coast-following jade shallows. Do not encode all materials into rigid RGB categories merely to obtain perfect colour-classification scores.
+- **Narrative:** actual saved missing spans and flooded streets stay in the rendering. Symbols communicate the drowned district at far scales; exact corridors and open rooms take over close up. Never add cranes to residential islands or invented wrecks to empty water.
+
+`paper-study.png` is the first round-two art direction study, retained because it was an input to the accepted overview. Its geometry is not authoritative. Its elastic finishing experiment was rejected for warping architecture. The production log records the subsequent corrections.

+## Current delivery: round two
+
+The original geographic pipeline below remains authoritative for source layers. The current art finish is **round2.py**, followed by **round2_balance.py**. Do not use the old `finish.py` entry point to export the round-two delivery: its all-features-at-all-scales treatment is the artistic behavior replaced in this round. Its registration/overlap helpers are still used for the close original paintings.
+
+Saved originals are sufficient to reproduce the current artwork; no image calls or downloads are needed when the base vectors and PNGs are present:
+
+```sh
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/reference.py
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2_restore.py
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 0
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 1
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 2
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 3
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2_balance.py
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2_measure.py
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/audit.py
+```
+
+Close-tile registration additionally needs the native 64-pixel geometry contexts. If `references/` was removed, run `round2_close_contexts.py` for z2 and the original `contexts.py 3` after a parent master exists. For z3, existing queue entries can prevent context regeneration; `round2_restore.py` reconstructs the geometry contexts without altering the historical used prompts and is the preferred clean-checkout path (run it immediately after `reference.py`). Contexts used for registration contain geometry, not the parent painting, so the generation-time parent is not needed to re-finish saved originals.
+
+| Round-two tool | Purpose |
+|---|---|
+| round2.py generalized 0 | Rebuild the overview's generalized plan from native vectors and spaced footprint anchors. The exact generation-time reference is also preserved as paintings/z0/geometry-input.png. |
+| round2.py contexts 1 | Prepare four generalized district references, parent crops and prompts for **new** image generation. Overwrites the z1 queue/prompts; not necessary for reproduction. |
+| round2_close_contexts.py | Prepare sixteen native neighborhood references and new district-parent crops; writes round2-queue.json. The accepted outputs replace z2 originals in place. |
+| round2.py finish Z | Continuous native canvas, scale-selected roads, geography-constrained coast, exposed rag paper, data-clipped architecture and district treatments. Keeps z3's original room paintings. Writes an ignored unbalanced-master.png and provisional final-master/tiles. |
+| round2_balance.py | Share broad RGB wash corrections across all four independent paintings without moving any ink geometry; cut final 1,024² tiles only after the continuous-canvas adjustment. |
+| round2_measure.py | All 140 separate tile joins, zero-loss reconstruction, adjacent-zoom RGB/8-pixel broad comparison, explicit limited pigment-boundary diagnostic, selected road support, and retained SHA-256 inventory. |
+| round2_restore.py | Recreate native registration contexts and review sheets from kept layers/originals/tiles. |

Raw downloads, references, warped copies and continuous finishing masters are ignored. No runtime/engine package or map file is produced.

+def assemble_far(z,w):

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.
+

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+| round2.py finish Z | Continuous native canvas, scale-selected roads, geography-constrained coast, exposed rag paper, data-clipped architecture and district treatments. Keeps z3's original room paintings. Writes an ignored unbalanced-master.png and provisional final-master/tiles. |
+| round2_balance.py | Share broad RGB wash corrections across all four independent paintings without moving any ink geometry; cut final 1,024² tiles only after the continuous-canvas adjustment. |
+| round2_measure.py | All 140 separate tile joins, zero-loss reconstruction, adjacent-zoom RGB/8-pixel broad comparison, explicit limited pigment-boundary diagnostic, selected road support, and retained SHA-256 inventory. |
+| round2_restore.py | Recreate native registration contexts and review sheets from kept layers/originals/tiles. |
+
+Measurements, production notes and delivery audit are retained under `assets/source/maps/miami/reports/`, and interpreted in `REPORT.md`. `checks/` contains only regenerable review pictures, external comparison copies, and experiments. Raw downloads, references, warped copies and continuous finishing masters are ignored. No runtime/engine package or map file is produced.
+
+The built-in image tool was used for every new raster painting. Exact prompts are beside the originals. The corrected z1 northeast original also has a correction prompt and its preceding source under `paintings/z1/studies/`. The first new overview study is retained under `style/` because it supplied art direction to the accepted overview. Foreign comparison images were inspected only, never passed to image generation. Generation itself is nondeterministic; the saved originals make finishing reproducible.

+def assemble_far(z,w):
+    n=len(w);g=64;s=1152

+    return out/np.maximum(total[...,None],1e-6)

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.
+

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.
+

+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2_restore.py
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 0
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 1
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 2
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 3
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2_balance.py
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2_measure.py
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/audit.py
+```
+
+Close-tile registration additionally needs the native 64-pixel geometry contexts. If `references/` was removed, run `round2_close_contexts.py` for z2 and the original `contexts.py 3` after a parent master exists. For z3, existing queue entries can prevent context regeneration; `round2_restore.py` reconstructs the geometry contexts without altering the historical used prompts and is the preferred clean-checkout path (run it immediately after `reference.py`). Contexts used for registration contain geometry, not the parent painting, so the generation-time parent is not needed to re-finish saved originals.
+
+| Round-two tool | Purpose |
+|---|---|
+| round2.py generalized 0 | Rebuild the overview's generalized plan from native vectors and spaced footprint anchors. The exact generation-time reference is also preserved as paintings/z0/geometry-input.png. |
+| round2.py contexts 1 | Prepare four generalized district references, parent crops and prompts for **new** image generation. Overwrites the z1 queue/prompts; not necessary for reproduction. |
+| round2_close_contexts.py | Prepare sixteen native neighborhood references and new district-parent crops; writes round2-queue.json. The accepted outputs replace z2 originals in place. |
+| round2.py finish Z | Continuous native canvas, scale-selected roads, geography-constrained coast, exposed rag paper, data-clipped architecture and district treatments. Keeps z3's original room paintings. Writes an ignored unbalanced-master.png and provisional final-master/tiles. |
+| round2_balance.py | Share broad RGB wash corrections across all four independent paintings without moving any ink geometry; cut final 1,024² tiles only after the continuous-canvas adjustment. |
+| round2_measure.py | All 140 separate tile joins, zero-loss reconstruction, adjacent-zoom RGB/8-pixel broad comparison, explicit limited pigment-boundary diagnostic, selected road support, and retained SHA-256 inventory. |
+| round2_restore.py | Recreate native registration contexts and review sheets from kept layers/originals/tiles. |
+
+Measurements, production notes and delivery audit are retained under `assets/source/maps/miami/reports/`, and interpreted in `REPORT.md`. `checks/` contains only regenerable review pictures, external comparison copies, and experiments. Raw downloads, references, warped copies and continuous finishing masters are ignored. No runtime/engine package or map file is produced.
+
+The built-in image tool was used for every new raster painting. Exact prompts are beside the originals. The corrected z1 northeast original also has a correction prompt and its preceding source under `paintings/z1/studies/`. The first new overview study is retained under `style/` because it supplied art direction to the accepted overview. Foreign comparison images were inspected only, never passed to image generation. Generation itself is nondeterministic; the saved originals make finishing reproducible.
+

+def assemble_far(z,w):
+    n=len(w);g=64;s=1152
+    out=np.zeros((n,n,3),np.float32);total=np.zeros((n,n),np.float32)
+    ramp=np.ones(s,np.float32);ramp[:128]=np.sin(np.linspace(0,np.pi/2,128))**2;ramp[-128:]=ramp[:128][::-1]
+    weight=ramp[:,None]*ramp[None,:];padded=np.pad(w,g,mode='edge')
+    for y in range(2**z):
+        for x in range(2**z):
+            p=ROOT/f'paintings/z{z}/{x}_{y}.raw.png'
+            a,info=far_register(load(p,(s,s)),padded[y*1024:y*1024+s,x*1024:x*1024+s])
+            p.with_name(f'{x}_{y}.registered.json').write_text(json.dumps(info,indent=2))
+            xa=max(0,x*1024-g);xb=min(n,(x+1)*1024+g);ya=max(0,y*1024-g);yb=min(n,(y+1)*1024+g)
+            u=xa-(x*1024-g);v=ya-(y*1024-g);q=weight[v:v+yb-ya,u:u+xb-xa]
+            out[ya:yb,xa:xb]+=a[v:v+yb-ya,u:u+xb-xa]*q[...,None];total[ya:yb,xa:xb]+=q
+    return out/np.maximum(total[...,None],1e-6)

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

"""Share broad-pigment differences between four independent continuous paintings.

No geometric resampling of final ink. Reductions are only used to estimate RGB
wash corrections; each native painting keeps its own high-frequency drawing.
"""
import json
import cv2
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from scipy import ndimage as nd
from common import ROOT


def scores(images):
    return [float(np.abs(nd.gaussian_filter(cv2.resize(images[z+1],(len(images[z]),)*2,interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)-images[z],(8,8,0))).mean()) for z in range(3)]


def main():
    images=[np.array(Image.open(ROOT/f'paintings/z{z}/unbalanced-master.png'),np.float32) for z in range(4)]
    log={'method':'symmetric continuous-canvas broad RGB wash relaxation, sigma 8 at each parent scale; native marks stay in place','initial':scores(images),'passes':[]}
    print('initial',log['initial'],flush=True)
    for step in range(14):
        # Alternate traversal prevents the last pair from dominating the chain.
        for z in ([2,1,0] if step%2==0 else [0,1,2]):
            parent=images[z];child=images[z+1];n=len(parent)
            small=cv2.resize(child,(n,n),interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)
            field=nd.gaussian_filter(small-parent,(8,8,0))
            field=np.clip(field,-12,12)
            parent+=field*.48
            # Chunking channel updates avoids a second full RGB 8k allocation.
            for k in range(3):
                big=cv2.resize(field[...,k],(n*2,n*2),interpolation=cv2.INTER_LINEAR)
                child[...,k]-=big*.52
            np.clip(parent,0,255,out=parent);np.clip(child,0,255,out=child)
        err=scores(images);log['passes'].append(err);print('pass',step+1,err,flush=True)
        if max(err)<1.65:break
    for z,a in enumerate(images):
        im=Image.fromarray(np.uint8(np.clip(np.rint(a),0,255)))
        im.save(ROOT/f'paintings/z{z}/final-master.png')
        for y in range(2**z):
            for x in range(2**z):im.crop((x*1024,y*1024,(x+1)*1024,(y+1)*1024)).save(ROOT/f'tiles/z{z}/{x}_{y}.png')
        im.resize((1024,1024),Image.Resampling.LANCZOS).save(ROOT/f'checks/overview_z{z}.png')
    log['final_float']=scores(images)
    (ROOT/'reports/round2-balance.json').write_text(json.dumps(log,indent=2))

if __name__=='__main__':main()

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.

+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)

# Miami — the drowned atlas

**Complete and accepted for this delivery.** Produced 2026-11-14, 17:28–19:38 UTC (about 2 h 10 min wall time). All 85 independently painted tiles, shared geographic layers, references, originals, prompts, measurements and reproduction tools are present.

## Delivery and geography

This is an original painted atlas of an **8,128 × 8,128 m** square: downtown and Brickell, the port, Biscayne Bay, the Venetian and other island chains, South Beach, Fisher Island, and northern Virginia Key. The projection is a local WGS84 Transverse Mercator centred at 25.78° N, 80.166° W, scale 1. Bounds are −4,064 to +4,064 m on both axes. North is up; grid/true-north convergence is below 0.018° at the edges.

| Corner | Longitude | Latitude |
|---|---:|---:|
| Northwest | −80.2065295168 | 25.8166780455 |
| Northeast | −80.1254704832 | 25.8166780455 |
| Southeast | −80.1254954055 | 25.7433104873 |
| Southwest | −80.2065045945 | 25.7433104873 |

| Zoom | Canvas | Tiles | Metres per pixel |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 1,024² | 1 | 7.9375 |
| 1 | 2,048² | 4 | 3.96875 |
| 2 | 4,096² | 16 | 1.984375 |
| 3 | 8,192² | 64 | 0.9921875 |

Every game tile is 1,024 × 1,024 RGB PNG, named `tiles/z<zoom>/<column>_<row>.png`, west to east and north to south. Tiles contain no lettering, border, compass or coordinate grid. `checks/viewer.html` provides an offline review viewer with optional separate overlays. `paintings/z*/final-master.png` stores the uncut canvases; `checks/overview_z*.png` provides small previews.

The engine foundation consists of 4,065 inclusive samples at 2 m spacing: exactly 4,064 cells, or 127 chunks of 64 m. Height is 16-bit PNG; classifications are 8-bit PNG. Canonical water, road, building and authored-canopy masks are additionally retained at 8,192² so narrow features survive world placement. [Layer encodings](base/VALUES.md) explain units, values, vertex versus image-pixel registration, and the normalized 0–100 overlay transform. `map.json` is the machine-readable geographic contract.

## Sources and fictional changes

[SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md) records addresses, licences, attribution and what was taken. [downloads.json](downloads.json) records exact requests, dates, byte counts and SHA-256 checksums. Downloads are ignored under `raw/`.

- NOAA's 2021 Miami-Dade bare-earth DEM: 369 intersecting tiles, CC0. Converted from NAVD88 US survey feet to metres. Valid coverage includes **99.9714% of source land samples**; 2,203 land samples are missing. Surveyed heights range from −5.53 to 17.18 m.
- Census TIGER/Line 2025: 38 clipped hydrography polygons and 1,184 road features, public domain/CC0. These define the shore and road centrelines.
- FEMA/ORNL USA Structures: 11,919 clipped building footprints. The federal catalogue describes a government work, but the delivery item declares CC BY 4.0. Attribution is retained conservatively; include SOURCES.md when redistributing.
- USGS NLCD 2021: public-domain land-cover classes at their actual approximately 30 m source resolution.

Road widths are authored corridors around the source centrelines. Future mangrove/reclamation, low street flooding, four broken causeway spans and four submerged wrecks are explicit world layers. Added tree crowns were frozen from the complete registered finest-scale paintings, then reused by every zoom: 6,878,251 fine pixels, with a 4,065-sample companion for the engine. These changes describe an invented future, not present-day surveys.

## How the painting was made

The original [style sheet](style/style-sheet.png) and [written style specification](style/STYLE.md) came first: ivory rag paper, warm quill ink, limestone ruins, olive foliage, mineral-teal water and pale jade shallows. No other game's map image or commercial basemap was supplied to image generation. The earlier project test was inspected as a quality comparison.

Each zoom received a newly rasterized geographic reference at its own resolution. All **85 tiles have a separately generated original painting**; none of the final zooms is a resized lower-level painting. The image tool returned approximately 1,254 px squares. Finer paintings include 64 px overlap around a 1,024 px tile, and were made against the native geometry, a crop of the accepted parent painting, and the shared style sheet. All original outputs, used prompts and context crops are preserved.

Image generation alone did not preserve geography. Finishing registers the pigment to geographic corners using position-constrained SIFT/RANSAC similarity fits, with a multistart main-water-silhouette fit in sparse scenes and a small smooth local shoreline correction. Original paint supplies washes, quill texture, foliage and ruin interiors. Exact native vector masks control every visible coast, road corridor and building silhouette. A continuous shallow wash repairs exposed water without dragging masonry or tree fragments into the bay. Interior ruin partitions are illustrative, not surveyed floorplans.

Overlapping paint is blended with smooth 128 px transitions on one continuous canvas per zoom. Geometry and colour finishing then run across the entire canvas before it is cut into tiles. Broad material-local pigment matching keeps parent colours stable while retaining separately painted close detail. The finest authored canopy is shared by all zooms and saved with world data.

The final format audit passed: **85 RGB 1,024² tiles, 85 original paintings, all required prompts, grayscale base layers with correct sizes and bit depths**, and SHA-256 inventory. Whole-map views, the complete 64-tile closest-scale sheet, native downtown/island/port/beach/mangrove tiles, and joined-corner crops were inspected. No visible tile joins or accidental lettering were found. See [zoom comparison](checks/zoom_comparison.jpg), [joined corners](checks/native_seams.jpg), and [all close-scale tiles](checks/final_z3.jpg).

The additional engine-grid check exposed a half-open polygon endpoint convention and surface-road/tunnel overlap. Endpoint classes and tunnel precedence were corrected. The **canonical fine masks have zero differing pixels and zero boundary error** against the finest geographic references. The 2 m companions still quantize narrow source features:

| 2 m companion versus finest vectors | IoU | 95th-percentile boundary distance | Maximum boundary distance |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| water | 0.998298 | 1 px | 4.000 px |
| roads | 0.907230 | 1 px | 23.195 px |
| buildings | 0.921490 | 1 px | 117.209 px |

The large maxima include very narrow/disappearing pieces and boundaries truncated by the map frame; they do not indicate a translation of the whole layer. **Do not use only the 2 m companions to reconstruct all fine outlines. Use `*_fine.png` or the supplied vectors for world feature placement.** Their finer resolution is necessary to preserve all source detail. The base height grid remains exactly 4,065².

Machine-readable results: [paint measurements](checks/measurements.json), [base-grid comparison](checks/base_grid_agreement.json), [delivery audit](checks/delivery_audit.json), and [endpoint corrections](checks/canonical_layers.json).

The geographic test classifies the final RGB pigments into water, roads and buildings, then compares those visible regions to native vector-derived masks. Water includes authored flooded streets; surface occlusion by bridges/buildings and authored bridge gaps is accounted for. These tests measure agreement with the supplied data, not the absolute surveying accuracy of that data. The distinct material palettes make the result directly inspectable; zero boundary error is a consequence of the constrained finish, not evidence that the image model traced perfectly.

Seam tests reconstruct every tile into its canvas and measure colour jumps at joins against nearby non-join boundaries. Parent comparisons use a 2× box reduction, with both raw RGB differences and an 8 px blurred comparison to separate native ink detail from broad colour agreement. Visual inspection remains necessary: correct masks alone did not catch the foliage and ghost-shoreline defects rejected during development.

## Artistic assessment and limits

The strongest result is the combination of Miami's distinctive island/port geometry with luminous water and fine, footprint-specific masonry. The pale street network remains legible beneath a game overlay; the closer drawings add room walls, courtyards, vegetation, flooded reaches and small wreck ribs without moving the world. Water-dominated tiles preserve open space.

The exact city fabric is denser at zoom 0 than a freely generalized explorer's atlas would be. That is the principal artistic compromise made to preserve every supplied building and road. Ruin interiors are symbolic, and some large structures still read as shaded masonry masses rather than fully exposed floorplans. Mangrove crowns are authored marks without surveyed heights. This is a map-art and shared-layer delivery, not a finished 3D terrain or building reconstruction.

TIGER is cartographic rather than a cadastral shoreline survey, FEMA omits some small structures, and source dates differ. Neither road widths nor individual tree crowns are measured. No bathymetry was acquired: missing DEM values use an explicit −1 m engine convention with a separate validity mask. Shallow-water colour is artistic and does not encode measured depth. NOAA point-cloud classifications and USGS 3DEP were not used because the selected DEM, footprints and land cover supplied the required layers.

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.
+

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

"""Scale-aware ink-and-wash finishing. Saved originals are the only paint inputs.

Round two intentionally separates semantic generalization from geographic precision.
Run `round2.py finish Z`, then `round2_measure.py`. See README for provenance.
"""
import argparse, json, math
import cv2
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
from scipy import ndimage as nd
from common import ROOT, SIZE, B, vectors, burn, save
from reference import grid_at
from finish import load, assemble, sample
from alignment import shore_align

PAPER=np.array([237,225,198],np.float32)
INK=np.array([80,73,51],np.float32)


def wet(a):
    return (a[...,1]-a[...,0]>3)&(a[...,2]-a[...,0]>-18)


def far_register(a,truth):
    """Silhouette-only fit avoids matching invented landmark windows to real blocks."""
    a,info=shore_align(a,truth)
    return a,info


def assemble_far(z,w):
    n=len(w);g=64;s=1152
    out=np.zeros((n,n,3),np.float32);total=np.zeros((n,n),np.float32)
    ramp=np.ones(s,np.float32);ramp[:128]=np.sin(np.linspace(0,np.pi/2,128))**2;ramp[-128:]=ramp[:128][::-1]
    weight=ramp[:,None]*ramp[None,:];padded=np.pad(w,g,mode='edge')
    for y in range(2**z):
        for x in range(2**z):
            p=ROOT/f'paintings/z{z}/{x}_{y}.raw.png'
            a,info=far_register(load(p,(s,s)),padded[y*1024:y*1024+s,x*1024:x*1024+s])
            p.with_name(f'{x}_{y}.registered.json').write_text(json.dumps(info,indent=2))
            xa=max(0,x*1024-g);xb=min(n,(x+1)*1024+g);ya=max(0,y*1024-g);yb=min(n,(y+1)*1024+g)
            u=xa-(x*1024-g);v=ya-(y*1024-g);q=weight[v:v+yb-ya,u:u+xb-xa]
            out[ya:yb,xa:xb]+=a[v:v+yb-ya,u:u+xb-xa]*q[...,None];total[ya:yb,xa:xb]+=q
    return out/np.maximum(total[...,None],1e-6)


def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.

    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
    """
    sw=wet(raw)
    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
    for k in range(3):
        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
    return clean,sw


def major_roads(z,n):
    water=np.array(Image.open(ROOT/f'references/z{z}/water.png'))>0
    chosen=[]
    for g,p in vectors('roads'):
        if 'tunl' in (p['name'] or '').lower():continue
        name=p['name'] or ''
        keep=p['mtfcc'] in ['S1100','S1200'] or any(t in name for t in ['Venetian','Dade Blvd'])
        if z==1: keep=keep or name in ['N Miami Ave','S Miami Ave','Washington Ave','Meridian Ave','West Ave','NE 2nd Ave','NW 2nd Ave']
        if z>=2:keep=True
        if keep:chosen.append((g.buffer(p['width_m']/2,cap_style=2,join_style=2),1))
    rd=burn(chosen,n)>0
    # Preserve every causeway, including local road sections over the bay.
    allrd=np.array(Image.open(ROOT/f'references/z{z}/roads.png'))>0
    rd|=allrd&water
    gaps=burn([(g,1) for g,p in vectors('future_changes') if p['kind']=='missing_bridge_span'],n)>0
    return rd&~gaps


def paper_texture(n):
    # Reuse original rag-paper tooth at every zoom; no new random noise field.
    sheet=load(ROOT/'style/style-sheet.png')
    swatch=sheet.mean(2)
    # Only subpixel tooth, never a strip containing drawn dune hatches. The
    # rejected small swatch repeated its strokes visibly across open water.
    swatch=np.clip(swatch-nd.gaussian_filter(swatch,.55),-4,4)*.50
    return np.tile(swatch,(math.ceil(n/swatch.shape[0]),math.ceil(n/swatch.shape[1])))[:n,:n]

    """Native geographic drawing plan: only principal roads and spaced anchors."""
    n=1024*2**z;ref=ROOT/f'references/z{z}'
    w=np.array(Image.open(ref/'surface_water.png'))>0

    g=(nd.gaussian_filter(green.astype(np.float32),4*2**z)>.25)&~w
    a[g]=[182,185,141];a[(bio==6)&~w]=[238,222,182]
    a[rd]=[220,206,173];a[(grid_at('flooded_streets',n)>0)&~w]=[123,159,144]
    a[w&~nd.binary_erosion(w)]=[95,99,68]
    selected=[]
    for geom,props in sorted(vectors('buildings'),key=lambda gp:-gp[0].area):
