def coasts(out,w,bio,z):
    """Subpixel wavering, interrupted ink and doubled quays on a continuous canvas."""
    n=len(w);mpp=SIZE/n
    dw=nd.distance_transform_edt(w).astype(np.float32)
    dl=nd.distance_transform_edt(~w).astype(np.float32)
    yy,xx=np.mgrid[:n,:n].astype(np.float32)
    # At most 0.8 pixel hand variation. Same world phase at all scales.
    u=xx/2**z;v=yy/2**z
    wave=.42*np.sin(u*.41+v*.28)+.24*np.sin(u*.93-v*.71)
    signed=dw-dl
    width=.70+.28*np.sin(u*.19+v*.23)+.22*np.sin(u*.69-v*.31)
    coast=np.maximum(0,1-np.abs(signed-wave)/(width+1.7))
    beach=nd.maximum_filter((bio==6).astype(np.float32),size=5)>0
    coast[beach]*=.15
    # Broken pen lift; never removes the true land/water division.
    lift=np.clip((np.sin(u*.31+v*.17)+.35)*1.5,0,1)
    alpha=coast*(.30+.52*lift)
    out=out*(1-alpha[...,None])+INK*alpha[...,None]
    # A second short stroke on the landward side of urban quays.
    quay=(~w)&(bio!=6)&~np.isin(bio,[3,4,5])
    double=np.exp(-((dl-2.2)/.5)**2)*quay*(np.sin(u*.17-v*.29)>.25)*.24
    out=out*(1-double[...,None])+INK*double[...,None]
    # Contour-following pale wash: land geometry controls every shallow.
    shall=np.exp(-dw/max(3,48/mpp))*w*.32
    out=out*(1-shall[...,None])+np.array([176,197,174])*shall[...,None]
    return out


def story(im,z,rd):
    """Only saved world objects: missing spans and wrecks, at exact locations."""
    n=im.width;mpp=SIZE/n;d=ImageDraw.Draw(im)
    def px(p):return ((p[0]-B[0])/mpp,(B[3]-p[1])/mpp)
    for g,p in vectors('future_changes'):
        if p['kind']=='submerged_wreck':
            pts=[px(t) for t in g.exterior.coords]
            d.line(pts,fill=(74,103,89),width=1)
            angle=math.radians(p['angle_degrees']);dx=math.cos(angle);dy=math.sin(angle)
            cx,cy=p['center'];length=p['length_m'];width=p['width_m']
            for u in np.arange(-length*.36,length*.35,max(5,mpp*1.6)):
                d.line([px((cx+u*dx-v*dy,cy+u*dy+v*dx)) for v in [-width*.45,width*.45]],fill=(77,102,84),width=1)
        elif p['kind']=='missing_bridge_span':
            # End-cap rubble remains inside existing surviving road pixels.
            gm=burn([(g.buffer(mpp*1.5),1)],n)>0
            arr=np.array(im);rim=gm&rd
            arr[rim]=arr[rim]*.48+INK*.52
            im=Image.fromarray(arr);d=ImageDraw.Draw(im)
    return im


def district_ink(out,z):
    """Data-clipped structural drawing: port trusses and beach-hotel galleries."""
    if z<2:return out
    from shapely.geometry import Polygon,LineString
    n=len(out);mpp=SIZE/n
    def world(u,v):return (B[0]+u*SIZE,B[3]-v*SIZE)
    port=Polygon([world(u,v) for u,v in [(.30,.49),(.77,.68),(.75,.70),(.55,.68),(.28,.56)]])
    im=Image.fromarray(np.uint8(np.clip(out,0,255)));d=ImageDraw.Draw(im)
    for geom,p in vectors('buildings'):
        if geom.area<650:continue
        c=geom.centroid;u=(c.x-B[0])/SIZE;v=(B[3]-c.y)/SIZE
        isport=port.contains(c)
        hotel=(u>.89 and .26<v<.73 and geom.area>1100)
        if not (isport or hotel):continue
        corners=np.array(geom.minimum_rotated_rectangle.exterior.coords)[:4]
        sides=np.roll(corners,-1,axis=0)-corners
        j=np.argmax(np.linalg.norm(sides,axis=1));long=sides[j];length=np.linalg.norm(long)
        long/=length;cross=np.array([-long[1],long[0]])
        projected=(corners-np.array([c.x,c.y]))@cross;width=np.ptp(projected)
        if length<25 or width<8:continue
        inner=geom.buffer(-1.5)
        for k,t in enumerate(np.arange(-length*.46,length*.47,11 if isport else 9)):
            if (k+p['id'])%5==0:continue # Missing structural bays, not roofs.
            center=np.array([c.x,c.y])+t*long
            endpoints=[center-cross*width*.48,center+cross*width*.48]
            if isport:endpoints[1]=endpoints[1]+long*4
            line=LineString(endpoints).intersection(inner)
            parts=list(line.geoms) if hasattr(line,'geoms') else [line]
            for part in parts:
                if part.geom_type!='LineString':continue
                pts=[((x-B[0])/mpp,(B[3]-y)/mpp) for x,y in part.coords]
                d.line(pts,fill=(125,99,67) if isport else (143,132,105),width=1)
    return np.asarray(im,dtype=np.float32)


def finish(z):
    n=1024*2**z;mpp=SIZE/n;ref=ROOT/f'references/z{z}'
    w=np.array(Image.open(ref/'surface_water.png'))>0
    b=np.array(Image.open(ref/'buildings.png'))>0
    bio=np.array(Image.open(ref/'biome.png'))
    rd=major_roads(z,n)
    if z==0:
        raw,info=far_register(load(ROOT/'paintings/z0/0_0.raw.png',(n,n)),w)
        (ROOT/'paintings/z0/0_0.registered.json').write_text(json.dumps(info,indent=2))
    elif z==1:
        raw=assemble_far(z,w)
    else:raw=assemble(z)
    save(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),ROOT/f'paintings/z{z}/registered.png')
    lum=raw.mean(2);fine=lum-nd.gaussian_filter(lum,.8)
    tooth=paper_texture(n)
    if z<=1:
        out,source_water=clean_far_coast(raw,w)
        # Fill wrongly painted water outside coast with paper only at coastline.
        dl=nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
        repair=(~w)&wet(out)&(dl<3)&~rd
        out[repair]=PAPER+fine[repair,None]*.35
    else:
        # Preserve the independently painted masonry, trees and courtyards.
        # Exposed substrate is now ivory with original rag tooth, not opaque tan.
        broad=nd.gaussian_filter(raw,(8,8,0))
        out=PAPER[None,None,:]*.72+broad*.28+tooth[...,None]
        nature=np.isin(bio,[3,4,5])
        canopy=np.array(Image.open(ROOT/'base/painted_canopy_fine.png').resize((n,n),Image.Resampling.NEAREST))>0
        nature=(nature|canopy)&~(w|b|rd)
        out[nature]=raw[nature]*.83+np.array([191,193,144])*.17
        # Sparse original drybrush in the paper, rather than all generated roads.
        dry=~(w|b|rd|nature)
        detail=np.clip(fine,-22,12)*.55
        out[dry]+=detail[dry,None]
        beach=(bio==6)&dry
        out[beach]=np.array([238,222,182])+fine[beach,None]*.55+tooth[beach,None]
        masonry=raw.copy()
        # Remove hue errors while allowing warm-grey walls, pale lime and ink.
        ml=masonry.mean(2)
        masonry=masonry*.85+np.stack([ml+10,ml+4,ml-12],-1)*.15
        db=nd.distance_transform_edt(b)
        edge=b&(db<=1)
        masonry[edge]=masonry[edge]*.44+INK*.56
        out[b]=masonry[b]
        # Distinct district treatment, anchored in world coordinates.
        yy,xx=np.mgrid[:n,:n].astype(np.float32);u=xx/n;v=yy/n
        port=(u>.29)&(u<.77)&(v>.49)&(v<.70)&b
        beachhotel=(u>.87)&(v>.28)&(v<.73)&b
        downtown=(u>.13)&(u<.28)&(v>.4)&(v<.79)&b
        out[port]=out[port]*.9+np.array([157,117,74])*.1
        out[beachhotel]=out[beachhotel]*.82+np.array([237,225,199])*.18
        out[downtown]*=.91
    # Paint continuous water from generated pigment, avoiding nearest-fill streaks.
    safe=nd.binary_erosion(wet(raw),iterations=7,border_value=1)&w
    sig=max(18,140/mpp);den=nd.gaussian_filter(safe.astype(np.float32),sig)
    water=raw.copy()
    feather=np.clip(nd.distance_transform_edt(safe)/12,0,1)
    for k in range(3):
        field=nd.gaussian_filter(raw[...,k]*safe,sig)/np.maximum(den,1e-5)
        field=np.where(den>.02,field,[113,153,143][k])
        if z<=1:
            detail=np.clip(raw[...,k]-nd.gaussian_filter(raw[...,k],2),-5,5)
            water[...,k]=field+detail*feather*.65+tooth*.45
        else:
            water[...,k]=raw[...,k]*feather+field*(1-feather)
    # Retain water tooth/current marks but suppress invented submerged objects.
    water=water*.86+np.array([146,174,158])*.14
    out[w]=water[w]
    # Major avenues only in far views; all native road corridors in close views.
    dr=nd.distance_transform_edt(rd)
    rpaint=np.array([235,222,190])+fine[...,None]*.30+tooth[...,None]
    edge=rd&(dr<=1)
    rpaint[edge]=rpaint[edge]*.85+INK*.15
    out[rd]=rpaint[rd]
    if z<=1:
        # Pictorial skyline ink occludes road ribbons as in an illustrated atlas.
        # This is symbol occlusion, not an alternate world-road alignment.
        yy,xx=np.mgrid[:n,:n];u=xx/n;v=yy/n
        skyline=(u>.08)&(u<.25)&(v>.32)&(v<.65)
        symbol=skyline&rd&(raw.mean(2)<155)&(raw[...,0]>raw[...,2]+20)
        out[symbol]=raw[symbol]
        # Preserve the cranes' elevated arms over water. Three local symbols,
        # each based on the new overview original, explicitly not coastline.
        if z==0:
            crane=np.zeros((n,n),bool)
            for x1,y1,x2,y2 in [(354,479,417,534),(462,529,521,582),(567,570,632,632)]:
                crane[y1:y2,x1:x2]=True
            crane &= (raw[...,0]-raw[...,1]>4)&(raw[...,1]-raw[...,2]>18)&(raw.mean(2)<190)
            out[crane]=raw[crane]
    flood=(grid_at('flooded_streets',n)>0)&~b
    # Flood remains the same world layer at every scale, with darker ink banks.
    out[flood]=np.array([123,159,144])+fine[flood,None]*.35
    out=district_ink(out,z)
    out=coasts(out,w,bio,z)
    if z>0:
        # Full RGB broad pigment agreement, separated by coast to avoid halos.
        parent=load(ROOT/f'paintings/z{z-1}/final-master.png',(n,n))
        for material,mask in [('water',w),('land',~w)]:
            mf=mask.astype(np.float32);sig=12;den=nd.gaussian_filter(mf,sig)
            for k in range(3):
                a=nd.gaussian_filter(out[...,k]*mf,sig)/np.maximum(den,.001)
                p=nd.gaussian_filter(parent[...,k]*mf,sig)/np.maximum(den,.001)
                if material=='land' and z>=2:
                    # A uniform pigment calibration avoids local glowing halos.
                    # The final multiscale pass shares the remaining broad error
                    # among the independent paintings, rather than forcing all
                    # of a distant icon's shadow into the closest ground wash.
                    delta=np.clip(np.mean(parent[...,k][mask])-np.mean(out[...,k][mask]),-12,12)
                    out[...,k][mask]+=delta
                else:
                    delta=np.clip(p-a,-100,100)*.98
                    out[...,k][mask]+=delta[mask]
    out=np.uint8(np.clip(out,0,255))
    im=story(Image.fromarray(out),z,rd)
    im.save(ROOT/f'paintings/z{z}/unbalanced-master.png')
    im.save(ROOT/f'paintings/z{z}/final-master.png')
    dest=ROOT/f'tiles/z{z}';dest.mkdir(parents=True,exist_ok=True)
    for y in range(2**z):
        for x in range(2**z):im.crop((x*1024,y*1024,(x+1)*1024,(y+1)*1024)).save(dest/f'{x}_{y}.png')
    im.resize((1024,1024),Image.Resampling.LANCZOS).save(ROOT/f'checks/overview_z{z}.png')
    save(rd.astype('uint8'),ref/'drawn_roads.png')
    print('round-two finish',z,flush=True)


if __name__=='__main__':
    p=argparse.ArgumentParser();p.add_argument('command',choices=['finish','contexts','generalized']);p.add_argument('zoom',type=int);a=p.parse_args()
    {'finish':finish,'contexts':contexts,'generalized':generalized}[a.command](a.zoom)

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

For z3, existing queue entries can prevent context regeneration; `round2_restore.py` reconstructs the geometry contexts without altering the historical used prompts and is the preferred clean-checkout path (run it immediately after `reference.py`). Contexts used for registration contain geometry, not the parent painting, so the generation-time parent is not needed to re-finish saved originals.
+
+| Round-two tool | Purpose |
+|---|---|
+| round2.py generalized 0 | Rebuild the overview's generalized plan from native vectors and spaced footprint anchors. The exact generation-time reference is also preserved as paintings/z0/geometry-input.png. |
+| round2.py contexts 1 | Prepare four generalized district references, parent crops and prompts for **new** image generation. Overwrites the z1 queue/prompts; not necessary for reproduction. |
+| round2_close_contexts.py | Prepare sixteen native neighborhood references and new district-parent crops; writes round2-queue.json. The accepted outputs replace z2 originals in place. |
+| round2.py finish Z | Continuous native canvas, scale-selected roads, geography-constrained coast, exposed rag paper, data-clipped architecture and district treatments. Keeps z3's original room paintings. Writes an ignored unbalanced-master.png and provisional final-master/tiles. |
+| round2_balance.py | Share broad RGB wash corrections across all four independent paintings without moving any ink geometry; cut final 1,024² tiles only after the continuous-canvas adjustment. |
+| round2_measure.py | All 140 separate tile joins, zero-loss reconstruction, adjacent-zoom RGB/8-pixel broad comparison, explicit limited pigment-boundary diagnostic, selected road support, and retained SHA-256 inventory. |
+| round2_restore.py | Recreate native registration contexts and review sheets from kept layers/originals/tiles. |
+
+Measurements, production notes and delivery audit are retained under `assets/source/maps/miami/reports/`, and interpreted in `REPORT.md`. `checks/` contains only regenerable review pictures, external comparison copies, and experiments. Raw downloads, references, warped copies and continuous finishing masters are ignored. No runtime/engine package or map file is produced.
+
+The built-in image tool was used for every new raster painting. Exact prompts are beside the originals. The corrected z1 northeast original also has a correction prompt and its preceding source under `paintings/z1/studies/`. The first new overview study is retained under `style/` because it supplied art direction to the accepted overview. Foreign comparison images were inspected only, never passed to image generation. Generation itself is nondeterministic; the saved originals make finishing reproducible.

+def assemble_far(z,w):

+            xa=max(0,x*1024-g);xb=min(n,(x+1)*1024+g);ya=max(0,y*1024-g);yb=min(n,(y+1)*1024+g)

+    return out/np.maximum(total[...,None],1e-6)

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

"""Delivery checks for generalized artwork; never label symbolic buildings as masks.

Measures every tile-edge segment independently (140 joins), exported RGB colour
agreement, true continuous-canvas cutting and source-drawn geometric support.
Visual findings and the limitations of these measurements belong in REPORT.md.
"""
import hashlib,json
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
from scipy import ndimage as nd
from common import ROOT
from reference import grid_at
from round2 import major_roads


def main():
    report={'method':'Round-two visible-RGB and support audit; generalized symbols are not footprint masks.','zooms':{}}
    hashes={};totaljoins=0
    for z in range(4):
        n=1024*2**z;master=ROOT/f'paintings/z{z}/final-master.png'
        a=np.array(Image.open(master));stitch=np.empty_like(a)
        for y in range(2**z):
            for x in range(2**z):
                p=ROOT/f'tiles/z{z}/{x}_{y}.png';im=Image.open(p)
                assert im.mode=='RGB' and im.size==(1024,1024)
                stitch[y*1024:(y+1)*1024,x*1024:(x+1)*1024]=im
                hashes[str(p.relative_to(ROOT))]=hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
        seams=[]
        for axis in ['vertical','horizontal']:
            v=a if axis=='vertical' else a.transpose(1,0,2)
            for k in range(1,2**z):
                c=k*1024
                for j in range(2**z):
                    s=v[j*1024:(j+1)*1024,c-33:c+34].astype(np.int16)
                    jumps=np.abs(np.diff(s,axis=1)).mean((0,2))
                    jump=float(jumps[32]);near=float(np.delete(jumps,32).mean())
                    seams.append({'axis':axis,'coordinate':c,'segment':j,'jump':jump,'nearby':near,'ratio':jump/max(near,.001)})
        totaljoins+=len(seams)
        result={'pixels':n,'tiles':4**z,'stitch_max_rgb_error':int(np.abs(a.astype(np.int16)-stitch).max()),'seams':seams}
        if z:
            small=np.asarray(Image.fromarray(a).resize((n//2,n//2),Image.Resampling.BOX),np.float32)
            par=np.asarray(Image.open(ROOT/f'paintings/z{z-1}/final-master.png'),np.float32)
            delta=small-par
            result['parent']={'raw_mae_255':float(np.abs(delta).mean()),'blur8_mae_255':float(np.abs(nd.gaussian_filter(delta,(8,8,0))).mean()),'mean_rgb_shift':delta.mean((0,1)).tolist(),'p95_channel_difference':float(np.percentile(np.abs(delta),95))}
        # Independent pigment classification of open water. Do not count distant
        # teal flood-wash inside symbolic districts as an invented ocean coast.
        ref=ROOT/f'references/z{z}'
        w=np.array(Image.open(ref/'surface_water.png'))>0
        af=a.astype(np.float32)
        observed=(af[...,1]-af[...,0]>3)&(af[...,2]-af[...,0]>-18)
        edge=w&~nd.binary_erosion(w,border_value=1)
        edge[[0,-1]]=False;edge[:,[0,-1]]=False
        obsedge=observed&~nd.binary_erosion(observed,border_value=1)
        dist=nd.distance_transform_edt(~obsedge)
        ds=dist[edge]
        # Ink can be dark-brown, so semantic pigment edges need not equal ink.
        result['water_pigment_boundary']={'mean_px':float(ds.mean()),'p95_px':float(np.percentile(ds,95)),'max_px':float(ds.max()),'fraction_within_2px':float(np.mean(ds<=2)), 'interpretation':'One-way proximity of source shore to teal pigment boundary; not a full coast IoU or proof of accuracy.'}
        rd=major_roads(z,n)
        saved=np.array(Image.open(ref/'drawn_roads.png'))>0
        result['road_render_support']={'differing_pixels':int((rd!=saved).sum()),'drawn_pixels':int(rd.sum()),'interpretation':'Exact selected vector corridors supplied to the painter, before illustrative occlusion, not RGB inference.'}
        land=~w
        paper=(af[...,0]>218)&(af[...,1]>205)&(af[...,2]>173)&land
        result['paper_fraction_of_land']=float(paper.sum()/land.sum())
        report['zooms'][f'z{z}']=result
        print(z,'joins',len(seams),'range',min([s['ratio'] for s in seams] or [0]),max([s['ratio'] for s in seams] or [0]),'parent',result.get('parent'),'shore',result['water_pigment_boundary'],flush=True)
    report['join_count']=totaljoins
    assert totaljoins==140
    (ROOT/'reports/round2-measurements.json').write_text(json.dumps(report,indent=2))
    for p in sorted((ROOT/'paintings').glob('z*/*.raw.png')):
        hashes[str(p.relative_to(ROOT))]=hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    for p in sorted((ROOT/'base').glob('*')):
        if p.is_file():hashes[str(p.relative_to(ROOT))]=hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    (ROOT/'reports/round2-sha256.json').write_text(json.dumps(hashes,indent=2))

if __name__=='__main__':main()

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.
+

+## Round two: scale and paper take priority
+
+The first finish lost the paper and forced all 11,919 footprints into every scale. The new overview and district originals use the same original style sheet with these stronger decisions:
+
+- **z0:** main avenues/causeways only; districts described by ivory intervals, loose wash and directional hatching. A small pictorial skyline, port sheds/cranes, courtyard ruins and beach hotels are representative district symbols. Their projected heights are illustrative; do not read a symbol's drawn silhouette as a surveyed building footprint.
+- **z1:** spaced source-building anchors and groups of ruins, more canals and park detail, still generous unpainted ground. Do not bring back the complete minor-road or house mesh.
+- **z2/z3:** the actual footprint fabric returns. Keep independently painted roofless rooms and vegetation; differentiate warehouse trusses, pale beach galleries, darker downtown masonry and low residential shells.
+- **Substrate:** exposed ivory, approximately #EDE1C6, with original rag tooth. The earlier land-wash anchor is a transparent pigment, never an opaque fill across all land. Quiet teal water may show paper tooth too.
+- **Coast:** a geographically constrained hand, with variable pressure, short pen lifts, doubled quay strokes, almost no outline across a beach, and coast-following jade shallows. Do not encode all materials into rigid RGB categories merely to obtain perfect colour-classification scores.
+- **Narrative:** actual saved missing spans and flooded streets stay in the rendering. Symbols communicate the drowned district at far scales; exact corridors and open rooms take over close up. Never add cranes to residential islands or invented wrecks to empty water.
+
+`paper-study.png` is the first round-two art direction study, retained because it was an input to the accepted overview. Its geometry is not authoritative. Its elastic finishing experiment was rejected for warping architecture. The production log records the subsequent corrections.

+Close-tile registration additionally needs the native 64-pixel geometry contexts. +
+| Round-two tool | Purpose |
+|---|---|
+| round2.py generalized 0 | Rebuild the overview's generalized plan from native vectors and spaced footprint anchors. The exact generation-time reference is also preserved as paintings/z0/geometry-input.png. |
+| round2.py contexts 1 | Prepare four generalized district references, parent crops and prompts for **new** image generation. Overwrites the z1 queue/prompts; not necessary for reproduction. |
+| round2_close_contexts.py | Prepare sixteen native neighborhood references and new district-parent crops; writes round2-queue.json. The accepted outputs replace z2 originals in place. |
+| round2.py finish Z | Continuous native canvas, scale-selected roads, geography-constrained coast, exposed rag paper, data-clipped architecture and district treatments. Keeps z3's original room paintings. Writes an ignored unbalanced-master.png and provisional final-master/tiles. |
+| round2_balance.py | Share broad RGB wash corrections across all four independent paintings without moving any ink geometry; cut final 1,024² tiles only after the continuous-canvas adjustment. |
+| round2_measure.py | All 140 separate tile joins, zero-loss reconstruction, adjacent-zoom RGB/8-pixel broad comparison, explicit limited pigment-boundary diagnostic, selected road support, and retained SHA-256 inventory. |
+| round2_restore.py | Recreate native registration contexts and review sheets from kept layers/originals/tiles. |

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.
+

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+For screen coordinates on the north-up picture, use eastward `u = 100×(E+4064)/8128` and southward `v = 100×(4064−N)/8128`, where `(E,N)` are our local projected easting/northing. +## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

import argparse
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image,ImageDraw
from common import ROOT


def contexts():
 for z in [2,3]:
  ref=ROOT/f'references/z{z}';im=Image.open(ref/'whole.png').convert('RGB')
  padded=Image.fromarray(np.pad(np.asarray(im),((64,64),(64,64),(0,0)),mode='edge'))
  for y in range(2**z):
   for x in range(2**z):padded.crop((x*1024,y*1024,x*1024+1152,y*1024+1152)).save(ref/f'{x}_{y}.context.png')
 print('restored geometry contexts',flush=True)

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.
+

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

# Shared world layers

Base PNGs without the `_fine` suffix are 4,065 × 4,065 **vertex samples**, with north at row 0. The inclusive endpoints span exactly 8,128 m: sample `(column,row)` is `(−4064 + 2×column, 4064 − 2×row)` metres in the local Transverse Mercator CRS in `../map.json`. There are 4,064 two-metre cells, 127 chunks of 64 m. Read grayscale values as numbers, with no color management or gamma conversion. The PNGs contain no georeferencing tags; `map.json` and this file are authoritative.

The game tile images instead use pixel areas: at zoom z, pixel centers are `(−4064 +(column+.5)×8128/(1024×2^z), 4064−(row+.5)×8128/(1024×2^z))`. This distinction prevents a half-pixel drift.

For screen coordinates on the north-up picture, use eastward `u = 100×(E+4064)/8128` and southward `v = 100×(4064−N)/8128`, where `(E,N)` are our local projected easting/northing. These are picture coordinates, **not engine x/z** and not geographic longitude/latitude. Overlay rendering belongs to the game; it is absent from every tile.

## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)

Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:

```text
engine.x = 4064 - E
engine.z = 4064 + N
engine.y = elevation_metres

E = 4064 - engine.x
N = engine.z - 4064
```

| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
|---|---|---|
| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |

Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.

Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.

Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

| File | Encoding |
|---|---|
| height.png | Unsigned 16-bit. Height in metres NAVD88 = value/100 − 100. NOAA heights converted from US survey feet with 1200/3937. Bilinear reprojection; 1 cm quantization. |
| height_valid.png | 8-bit: 255 surveyed DEM coverage; 0 absent. Missing heights use −1 m in height.png. **This is an explicit engine convention, not measured bathymetry.** |
| water.png | 8-bit: 1 TIGER water polygon; 0 land. Water beneath elevated bridges is retained. |
| roads.png | 8-bit: 0 none; 1 local/service/path; 2 arterial/highway; 3 road over source water; 4 subterranean tunnel (not painted as a surface bridge); 5 authored missing bridge span. TIGER centerlines are measured geometry; corridor widths are authored: 22 m highway, 14 m arterial, 8 m local, 3–7 m paths/ramps/service. |
| buildings.png | 8-bit: 1 footprint; 0 outside. FEMA/ORNL USA Structures. Includes actual courtyards/holes where supplied. |
| landcover.png | 8-bit NLCD 2021 codes, nearest sampling. 11 water; 21 developed open; 22 low-intensity development; 23 medium; 24 high; 31 barren; 41 deciduous forest; 42 evergreen; 43 mixed; 52 shrub; 71 grass; 81 pasture; 82 crops; 90 woody wetland; 95 emergent wetland; 255 source nodata. Native source is ~30 m, not 2 m. |
| biome.png | Authored succession: 1 water; 2 open urban land; 3 reclaimed vegetation; 4 coastal mangrove; 5 low wetland; 6 sand; 7 ruin footprint; 8 road; 9 bridge. Derived from NLCD, DEM, shore distance and exact geometry. These are fictional future conditions, not surveyed present vegetation. |
| flooded_streets.png | Authored standing water: 1 low street pool; 0 other. Road land below 0.55 m NAVD88, within 300 m of the surveyed coast, excluding buildings; small artifacts removed. Coast geometry is unchanged. |
| bridge_gaps.png | Authored missing spans: 1 gap region; 0 other. Intersect with road-over-water to remove the deck. Four precise vector polygons are in future_changes.geojson. |
| wrecks.png | Authored submerged hulls: 1 footprint; 0 other. Four original fictional objects, not recorded real wreck sites. Positions and outlines in future_changes.geojson; the water above them remains water. |
| painted_canopy.png | 8-bit: 1 added future-world vegetation crown; 0 other. Authored from the registered finest-scale original paintings, excluding water, roads, buildings and beach. Union with biome vegetation classes 3–5 for world placement. Not a tree survey and does not encode heights. |

Four files use a finer grid: `water_fine.png`, `buildings_fine.png`, `roads_fine.png`, and `painted_canopy_fine.png` are 8,192 × 8,192 pixel areas across the same bounds. They use the same respective class encodings. **Use these canonical fine masks or the vectors for world feature placement:** very thin source features can disappear between 2 m samples. These masks supply the finest painting's geometric support; round-two shore ink may thicken, thin and waver within the narrow finishing band. The 4,065-sample layers are convenient engine-grid companions, not a lossless substitute for the fine outlines.

The fine canopy preserves close-scale crown outlines and controls vegetation in the round-two z2/z3 finish. The far views use generalized district wash and representative palm/grove symbols, not individually placed tree crowns. `painted_canopy.json` records provenance and counts. At the inclusive grid's four outer sample lines, classifications use the adjacent finest pixel inside the square, avoiding a false empty fringe caused by half-open polygon rasterization. `../reports/canonical-layers.json` records endpoint corrections. Road tunnels occupy class 4 only where there is no visible surface road; an intersecting surface road retains its surface class.

`areawater.geojson`, `roads.geojson` and `buildings.geojson` retain clipped vector geometry in the **local projected CRS**, not RFC 7946 geographic degrees. Their `crs` member declares it. Use them to render reference images afresh at every zoom. Do not enlarge the 2 m masks for close-scale shoreline tracing.

Known source limits: TIGER is cartographic rather than a modern cadastral coastline survey; FEMA excludes many structures below 450 square feet and does not certify sub-metre positional accuracy. A 1 px painting-registration score measures agreement with these inputs, not their accuracy on Earth. Source dates differ. No ocean bathymetry has been acquired.

Offline source/art tools only. They add no dependency to the engine or its build.

## Current delivery: round two

The original geographic pipeline below remains authoritative for source layers. The current art finish is **round2.py**, followed by **round2_balance.py**. Do not use the old `finish.py` entry point to export the round-two delivery: its all-features-at-all-scales treatment is the artistic behavior replaced in this round. Its registration/overlap helpers are still used for the close original paintings.

Saved originals are sufficient to reproduce the current artwork; no image calls or downloads are needed when the base vectors and PNGs are present:

```sh
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/reference.py
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2_restore.py
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 0
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 1

tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2_balance.py
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2_measure.py
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/audit.py
```

Close-tile registration additionally needs the native 64-pixel geometry contexts. If `references/` was removed, run `round2_close_contexts.py` for z2 and the original `contexts.py 3` after a parent master exists. For z3, existing queue entries can prevent context regeneration; `round2_restore.py` reconstructs the geometry contexts without altering the historical used prompts and is the preferred clean-checkout path (run it immediately after `reference.py`). Contexts used for registration contain geometry, not the parent painting, so the generation-time parent is not needed to re-finish saved originals.

Raw downloads, references, warped copies and continuous finishing masters are ignored. No runtime/engine package or map file is produced.

The built-in image tool was used for every new raster painting. Exact prompts are beside the originals. The corrected z1 northeast original also has a correction prompt and its preceding source under `paintings/z1/studies/`. The first new overview study is retained under `style/` because it supplied art direction to the accepted overview. Foreign comparison images were inspected only, never passed to image generation. Generation itself is nondeterministic; the saved originals make finishing reproducible.

## Original geographic preparation and round-one tools

From the repository root, create the isolated environment:

```sh
python3 -m venv tools/mapart/.venv
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/pip install -r tools/mapart/requirements.txt
```

The frozen bounds, projection and sample conventions are in `assets/source/maps/miami/map.json`. Python 3.9 was used; exact package versions are pinned. Raw data and the virtual environment are ignored by git.

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| fetch.py | Download intersecting NOAA DEM tiles, county TIGER ZIPs, NLCD coverage and paginated FEMA footprints. Write exact request URLs and SHA-256 checksums to downloads.json. Reuses existing downloads. |
| prepare.py | Clip/reproject vectors, reproject bare-earth height, rasterize 4,065 vertex samples, preserve NLCD codes, author explicit succession and low-street flooding. Checks FEMA pages against the complete object-ID inventory. |
| future.py | Freeze four missing bridge spans and four submerged wrecks as shared world geometry; mark tunnels as subterranean. Run after prepare.py. |
| reference.py [zooms...] | Render geographic references afresh from the vector data at each native zoom, with water/road/building masks. Default: all four zooms. |
| contexts.py Z | Build each tile's 64 px neighboring overlap, parent-paint context, exact prompt and queue.json for the built-in image tool. |
| finish.py Z | Similarity registration, local shoreline registration, class-constrained pigment and architectural detail, overlapping assembly, parent-color matching, exact cutting into 1,024 px PNGs. Requires every original painting for that zoom. |
| finish.py Z --partial | Pilot only: export already-painted tiles while keeping explicitly provisional parent proxies under checks/partial_zZ.png. Never use partial images as a completed delivery. |
| alignment.py | Position-constrained SIFT/RANSAC registration of original ink against geographic corners, with multistart main-water-silhouette similarity fitting for sparse scenes. Used by finish.py; cache metadata retains fit residuals and transforms. |
| preregister.py Z --watch | Populate registration caches as originals arrive. Stops when that zoom is complete; does not export tiles. |
| author_canopy.py | Freeze vegetation crowns from the complete registered zoom-3 painting as shared fictional world layers. Run once, then finish zooms 0 through 3 in order. |
| canonical.py | Save 8,192 px canonical water/road/building masks; repair classifications at inclusive outer grid samples and preserve surface roads over tunnels. Run after native references. |
| measure.py | Independently classify visible features from exported RGB; measure IoU, symmetric boundary distances, exact tile reconstruction, seam jumps, and parent-scale color differences. |
| grid_check.py | Quantify the difference between the engine's 2 m vertex samples and the finest native vector masks, independently of artwork. |
| review.py Z reference/raw/final [--row R] | Labeled contact sheets for review, under checks; never adds labels to game tiles. |
| audit.py | Assert tile count, RGB format, original-paint presence, base dimensions and bit depth; hash delivery artifacts. |

Build sources and references:

```sh
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/fetch.py
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/prepare.py
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/future.py
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/reference.py
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/canonical.py
```

Image generation is an explicit art-production step using the **built-in image tool**, not an API-key script. The overview prompt is under paintings/z0; later queues are made by contexts.py. Each queue entry lists its geometry reference, accepted parent, original style sheet and output filename. Inspect inputs, issue the prompt with those local references, then copy the returned original PNG to `paintings/zZ/C_R.raw.png`. Preserve supplementary prompt files. Do not resize or overwrite the raw originals. The tool returned 1,254 px squares during this run. The finishing code maps each to its 1,152 px overlap region (or 1,024 px overview).

After a complete zoom is painted:

```sh
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/finish.py 1
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/measure.py
tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/contexts.py 2
```

Review the full map, representative full-resolution tiles, and joined boundaries. Exact geometry measurements do not establish artistic quality. Never accept solely on an RGB-mask score.

The offline viewer is `assets/source/maps/miami/checks/viewer.html`; open it directly in a browser. It reads the actual PNG tiles, supports pan/zoom and a fixed-camera painting comparison, and draws optional diagnostic overlays independently. No server or dependencies are required.

For final acceptance after every original exists, run `finish.py 3`, `author_canopy.py`, then `finish.py 0`, `finish.py 1`, `finish.py 2`, `finish.py 3`, `measure.py`, `grid_check.py` and `audit.py`. Preserve the frozen canopy during later finishing runs. `contexts.py` leaves prompts and reference crops for already-painted tiles intact. Exact fresh image generation is nondeterministic; the saved originals make subsequent finishing reproducible.

Do not change map.json after downloading and preparing an accepted map. To explore different bounds, use a separate destination and manifest: the download cache filenames describe this frozen square. See SOURCES.md and base/VALUES.md for source limits, licensing and authored-world conventions.

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.
+

+

+- **Substrate:** exposed ivory, approximately #EDE1C6, with original rag tooth. The earlier land-wash anchor is a transparent pigment, never an opaque fill across all land. Quiet teal water may show paper tooth too.
+- **Coast:** a geographically constrained hand, with variable pressure, short pen lifts, doubled quay strokes, almost no outline across a beach, and coast-following jade shallows. Do not encode all materials into rigid RGB categories merely to obtain perfect colour-classification scores.
+- **Narrative:** actual saved missing spans and flooded streets stay in the rendering. Symbols communicate the drowned district at far scales; exact corridors and open rooms take over close up. Never add cranes to residential islands or invented wrecks to empty water.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+| round2.py finish Z | Continuous native canvas, scale-selected roads, geography-constrained coast, exposed rag paper, data-clipped architecture and district treatments. Keeps z3's original room paintings. Writes an ignored unbalanced-master.png and provisional final-master/tiles. |
+| round2_balance.py | Share broad RGB wash corrections across all four independent paintings without moving any ink geometry; cut final 1,024² tiles only after the continuous-canvas adjustment. |
+| round2_measure.py | All 140 separate tile joins, zero-loss reconstruction, adjacent-zoom RGB/8-pixel broad comparison, explicit limited pigment-boundary diagnostic, selected road support, and retained SHA-256 inventory. |
+| round2_restore.py | Recreate native registration contexts and review sheets from kept layers/originals/tiles. |
+
+Measurements, production notes and delivery audit are retained under `assets/source/maps/miami/reports/`, and interpreted in `REPORT.md`. `checks/` contains only regenerable review pictures, external comparison copies, and experiments. Raw downloads, references, warped copies and continuous finishing masters are ignored. No runtime/engine package or map file is produced.
+
+The built-in image tool was used for every new raster painting. Exact prompts are beside the originals. The corrected z1 northeast original also has a correction prompt and its preceding source under `paintings/z1/studies/`. The first new overview study is retained under `style/` because it supplied art direction to the accepted overview. Foreign comparison images were inspected only, never passed to image generation. Generation itself is nondeterministic; the saved originals make finishing reproducible.

+def assemble_far(z,w):
+    n=len(w);g=64;s=1152

+    return out/np.maximum(total[...,None],1e-6)

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+"""Scale-legible wreck symbols at saved world positions, not enlarged world hulls."""
+import math
+from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
+from common import B, SIZE, vectors
+
+
+def wreck_symbols(im, z):
+    if z > 1:
+        return im
+    scale = 4
+    layer = Image.new('RGBA', (im.width*scale, im.height*scale))
+    d = ImageDraw.Draw(layer)
+    mpp = SIZE/im.width
+    for _, p in vectors('future_changes'):
+        if p['kind'] != 'submerged_wreck':
+            continue
+        cx = (p['center'][0]-B[0])/mpp
+        cy = (B[3]-p['center'][1])/mpp
+        angle = -math.radians(p['angle_degrees'])
+        length = max(p['length_m']/mpp, 14 if z == 0 else 18)
+        width = max(p['width_m']/mpp, 4.5 if z == 0 else 5.5)
+        def point(u, v):
+            x = u*length; y = v*width
+            return ((cx+x*math.cos(angle)-y*math.sin(angle))*scale,
+                    (cy+x*math.sin(angle)+y*math.cos(angle))*scale)
+        hull = [(-.5,0),(-.35,-.44),(.22,-.5),(.5,0),(.22,.5),(-.35,.44)]
+        d.polygon([point(*q) for q in hull], fill=(100,125,108,225))
+        # One torn gunwale, rusted stem and pale exposed frames.
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[:4]], fill=(74,76,53,242), width=3)
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[4:]+[hull[0]]], fill=(82,84,60,220), width=2)
+        for i, u in enumerate([-.29,-.13,.05,.23]):
+            d.line([point(u,-.34),point(u,.31 if i!=2 else .1)],
+                   fill=(205,197,153,238), width=2)
+        d.line([point(.18,0),point(.46,0)], fill=(137,104,62,245), width=3)
+    layer = layer.resize(im.size, Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
+    return Image.alpha_composite(im.convert('RGBA'),layer).convert('RGB')

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.
+

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+"""Scale-legible wreck symbols at saved world positions, not enlarged world hulls."""
+import math
+from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
+from common import B, SIZE, vectors
+
+
+def wreck_symbols(im, z):
+    if z > 1:
+        return im
+    scale = 4
+    layer = Image.new('RGBA', (im.width*scale, im.height*scale))
+    d = ImageDraw.Draw(layer)
+    mpp = SIZE/im.width
+    for _, p in vectors('future_changes'):
+        if p['kind'] != 'submerged_wreck':
+            continue
+        cx = (p['center'][0]-B[0])/mpp
+        cy = (B[3]-p['center'][1])/mpp
+        angle = -math.radians(p['angle_degrees'])
+        length = max(p['length_m']/mpp, 14 if z == 0 else 18)
+        width = max(p['width_m']/mpp, 4.5 if z == 0 else 5.5)
+        def point(u, v):
+            x = u*length; y = v*width
+            return ((cx+x*math.cos(angle)-y*math.sin(angle))*scale,
+                    (cy+x*math.sin(angle)+y*math.cos(angle))*scale)
+        hull = [(-.5,0),(-.35,-.44),(.22,-.5),(.5,0),(.22,.5),(-.35,.44)]
+        d.polygon([point(*q) for q in hull], fill=(100,125,108,225))
+        # One torn gunwale, rusted stem and pale exposed frames.
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[:4]], fill=(74,76,53,242), width=3)
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[4:]+[hull[0]]], fill=(82,84,60,220), width=2)
+        for i, u in enumerate([-.29,-.13,.05,.23]):
+            d.line([point(u,-.34),point(u,.31 if i!=2 else .1)],
+                   fill=(205,197,153,238), width=2)
+        d.line([point(.18,0),point(.46,0)], fill=(137,104,62,245), width=3)
+    layer = layer.resize(im.size, Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
+    return Image.alpha_composite(im.convert('RGBA'),layer).convert('RGB')

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+"""Scale-legible wreck symbols at saved world positions, not enlarged world hulls."""
+import math
+from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
+from common import B, SIZE, vectors
+
+
+def wreck_symbols(im, z):
+    if z > 1:
+        return im
+    scale = 4
+    layer = Image.new('RGBA', (im.width*scale, im.height*scale))
+    d = ImageDraw.Draw(layer)
+    mpp = SIZE/im.width
+    for _, p in vectors('future_changes'):
+        if p['kind'] != 'submerged_wreck':
+            continue
+        cx = (p['center'][0]-B[0])/mpp
+        cy = (B[3]-p['center'][1])/mpp
+        angle = -math.radians(p['angle_degrees'])
+        length = max(p['length_m']/mpp, 14 if z == 0 else 18)
+        width = max(p['width_m']/mpp, 4.5 if z == 0 else 5.5)
+        def point(u, v):
+            x = u*length; y = v*width
+            return ((cx+x*math.cos(angle)-y*math.sin(angle))*scale,
+                    (cy+x*math.sin(angle)+y*math.cos(angle))*scale)
+        hull = [(-.5,0),(-.35,-.44),(.22,-.5),(.5,0),(.22,.5),(-.35,.44)]
+        d.polygon([point(*q) for q in hull], fill=(100,125,108,225))
+        # One torn gunwale, rusted stem and pale exposed frames.
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[:4]], fill=(74,76,53,242), width=3)
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[4:]+[hull[0]]], fill=(82,84,60,220), width=2)
+        for i, u in enumerate([-.29,-.13,.05,.23]):
+            d.line([point(u,-.34),point(u,.31 if i!=2 else .1)],
+                   fill=(205,197,153,238), width=2)
+        d.line([point(.18,0),point(.46,0)], fill=(137,104,62,245), width=3)
+    layer = layer.resize(im.size, Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
+    return Image.alpha_composite(im.convert('RGBA'),layer).convert('RGB')

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
+
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.
