+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+"""Scale-legible wreck symbols at saved world positions, not enlarged world hulls."""
+import math
+from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
+from common import B, SIZE, vectors
+
+
+def wreck_symbols(im, z):
+    if z > 1:
+        return im
+    scale = 4
+    layer = Image.new('RGBA', (im.width*scale, im.height*scale))
+    d = ImageDraw.Draw(layer)
+    mpp = SIZE/im.width
+    for _, p in vectors('future_changes'):
+        if p['kind'] != 'submerged_wreck':
+            continue
+        cx = (p['center'][0]-B[0])/mpp
+        cy = (B[3]-p['center'][1])/mpp
+        angle = -math.radians(p['angle_degrees'])
+        length = max(p['length_m']/mpp, 14 if z == 0 else 18)
+        width = max(p['width_m']/mpp, 4.5 if z == 0 else 5.5)
+        def point(u, v):
+            x = u*length; y = v*width
+            return ((cx+x*math.cos(angle)-y*math.sin(angle))*scale,
+                    (cy+x*math.sin(angle)+y*math.cos(angle))*scale)
+        hull = [(-.5,0),(-.35,-.44),(.22,-.5),(.5,0),(.22,.5),(-.35,.44)]
+        d.polygon([point(*q) for q in hull], fill=(100,125,108,225))
+        # One torn gunwale, rusted stem and pale exposed frames.
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[:4]], fill=(74,76,53,242), width=3)
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[4:]+[hull[0]]], fill=(82,84,60,220), width=2)
+        for i, u in enumerate([-.29,-.13,.05,.23]):
+            d.line([point(u,-.34),point(u,.31 if i!=2 else .1)],
+                   fill=(205,197,153,238), width=2)
+        d.line([point(.18,0),point(.46,0)], fill=(137,104,62,245), width=3)
+    layer = layer.resize(im.size, Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
+    return Image.alpha_composite(im.convert('RGBA'),layer).convert('RGB')

"""Register generated pigment, then constrain every visible feature to world geometry."""
import argparse,json,hashlib,inspect
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image,ImageDraw
from scipy import ndimage as nd
from common import *
from reference import grid_at
from alignment import feature_align,shore_align

def load(path,size=None):
    im=Image.open(path).convert('RGB')
    if size:im=im.resize(size,Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
    return np.asarray(im,dtype=np.float32)

def water_rgb(a):return (a[...,1]-a[...,0]>3)&(a[...,2]-a[...,0]>-18)

def sample(a,y,x):
    if a.ndim==2:return nd.map_coordinates(a,[y,x],order=1,mode='nearest')
    return np.stack([nd.map_coordinates(a[...,i],[y,x],order=1,mode='nearest') for i in range(3)],-1)

def register(a,truth,reference=None):
    """Small smooth shoreline correction; final geometry is imposed separately."""
    aligned=False
    register.last_info={}
    if reference is not None:
        a,aligned,info=feature_align(a,reference)
        register.last_info['feature_fit']=info
        print('features',info,flush=True)
    if not aligned and .002<truth.mean()<.998:
        a,info=shore_align(a,truth)
        register.last_info['shore_similarity']=info
        print('shore similarity',info,flush=True)
        aligned=True
    if not aligned and a.shape[0]==1152:
        # Measured fallback for this image tool's expanded framing. Broad water
        # scenes lack unique corners; allow only small shoreline refinements.
        y,x=np.mgrid[:1152,:1152].astype(np.float32)
        a=sample(a,y/1.082,x/1.082)
    wet=water_rgb(a)
    ss=nd.gaussian_filter(nd.distance_transform_edt(wet)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~wet),1)
    ts=nd.gaussian_filter(nd.distance_transform_edt(truth)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~truth),1)
    sy,sx=np.gradient(ss)
    yy,xx=np.mgrid[:truth.shape[0],:truth.shape[1]].astype(np.float32)
    ux=np.zeros_like(xx);uy=np.zeros_like(yy)
    band=np.exp(-(np.abs(ts)/24)**4)
    for _ in range(12):
        delta=ts-sample(ss,yy+uy,xx+ux)
        gy=sample(sy,yy+uy,xx+ux);gx=sample(sx,yy+uy,xx+ux)
        den=gx*gx+gy*gy+(delta/2)**2+1e-4
        ux=nd.gaussian_filter(ux+nd.gaussian_filter(delta*gx/den,1)*band,.65)
        uy=nd.gaussian_filter(uy+nd.gaussian_filter(delta*gy/den,1)*band,.65)
        ux=np.clip(ux,-4,4);uy=np.clip(uy,-4,4)
    a=sample(a,yy+uy,xx+ux)
    # Repair only water, using open-water pigment clear of any inked land.
    # Keep land's original brushwork intact; semantic palettes handle invented
    # inland pools later without nearest-neighbor patchwork across tree crowns.
    wet=water_rgb(a)
    safe=nd.binary_erosion(wet,iterations=10,border_value=1)
    if safe.any():
        inds=nd.distance_transform_edt(~safe,return_distances=False,return_indices=True)
        bad=truth&~safe
        a[bad]=a[inds[0][bad],inds[1][bad]]
        smooth=nd.gaussian_filter(a,(1.6,1.6,0))
        blend=nd.gaussian_filter(bad.astype(np.float32),1.6)*truth
        a=a*(1-blend[...,None])+smooth*blend[...,None]
    return a

def cached_register(path,reference_path,truth,size):
    cache=path.with_name(path.name.replace('.raw.png','.registered.png'))
    meta=cache.with_suffix('.json')
    fingerprint=hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()+reference_path.read_bytes()+truth.tobytes()+
          inspect.getsource(register).encode()+inspect.getsource(feature_align).encode()+inspect.getsource(shore_align).encode()).hexdigest()
    if cache.exists() and meta.exists() and json.loads(meta.read_text()).get('fingerprint')==fingerprint:
        return load(cache)
    a=register(load(path,(size,size)),truth,load(reference_path))
    save(np.uint8(np.clip(a,0,255)),cache)
    meta.write_text(json.dumps({'fingerprint':fingerprint,'raw':path.name,**register.last_info},indent=2))
    return load(cache)

def assemble(z,partial=False):
    n=1024*2**z;count=2**z; ref=ROOT/'references'/f'z{z}'
    truth=np.array(Image.open(ref/'surface_water.png'))>0
    if z==0:return cached_register(ROOT/'paintings/z0/0_0.raw.png',ref/'whole.png',truth,n)
    # Overlapping native-scale paintings; smooth partition of unity in the gutters.
    out=np.zeros((n,n,3),np.float32);total=np.zeros((n,n),np.float32)
    g=64;size=1024+2*g
    ramp=np.ones(size,np.float32);ramp[:2*g]=np.sin(np.linspace(0,np.pi/2,2*g))**2
    ramp[-2*g:]=ramp[:2*g][::-1]
    weight=ramp[:,None]*ramp[None,:]
    padded=np.pad(truth,g,mode='edge')
    for y in range(count):
        for x in range(count):
            p=ROOT/'paintings'/f'z{z}'/f'{x}_{y}.raw.png'
            if not p.exists():
                if not partial:raise FileNotFoundError(p)
                continue
            target=padded[y*1024:y*1024+size,x*1024:x*1024+size]
            a=cached_register(p,ref/f'{x}_{y}.context.png',target,size)
            xa=max(0,x*1024-g);xb=min(n,(x+1)*1024+g)
            ya=max(0,y*1024-g);yb=min(n,(y+1)*1024+g)
            u=xa-(x*1024-g);v=ya-(y*1024-g)
            w=weight[v:v+yb-ya,u:u+xb-xa].copy()
            if x==0:w[:,:g]=ramp[v:v+yb-ya,None]
            if y==0:w[:g,:]=ramp[None,u:u+xb-xa]
            if x==count-1:w[:,-g:]=ramp[v:v+yb-ya,None]
            if y==count-1:w[-g:,:]=ramp[None,u:u+xb-xa]
            if x==0 and y==0:w[:g,:g]=1
            if x==count-1 and y==0:w[:g,-g:]=1
            if x==0 and y==count-1:w[-g:,:g]=1
            if x==count-1 and y==count-1:w[-g:,-g:]=1
            out[ya:yb,xa:xb]+=a[v:v+yb-ya,u:u+xb-xa]*w[...,None]
            total[ya:yb,xa:xb]+=w
    out/=np.maximum(total[...,None],1e-6)
    if partial:
        parent_path=ROOT/'paintings'/f'z{z-1}'/'final-master.png'
        if not parent_path.exists():parent_path=ROOT/'checks'/f'partial_z{z-1}.png'
        parent=load(parent_path,(n,n));missing=total<.999
        out[missing]=out[missing]*total[missing,None]+parent[missing]*(1-total[missing,None])
    return out

def pigment(lum,rg,gb):
    # Distinct physical pigment families make geometry measurable directly in RGB.
    g=np.clip(lum,gb+2,253-rg)
    return np.stack([g+rg,g,g-gb],-1)

def finish(z,partial=False):
    n=1024*2**z;mpp=SIZE/n; ref=ROOT/'references'/f'z{z}'
    raw=assemble(z,partial)
    save(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),ROOT/'paintings'/f'z{z}'/'registered.png')
    w=np.array(Image.open(ref/'surface_water.png'))>0
    rd=np.array(Image.open(ref/'roads.png'))>0
    b=np.array(Image.open(ref/'buildings.png'))>0
    bio=np.array(Image.open(ref/'biome.png'))
    # Remove invented architectural boundaries, retain gently varying wash.
    l=raw.mean(2);soft=nd.gaussian_filter(l,2.2+z*.65)
    fine=np.clip(l-nd.gaussian_filter(l,.65),-22,22)
    # Bare paper receives a broad wash, not blurred ghosts of generated trees or
    # invented houses. Crisp detail is reserved for the constrained feature masks.
    paper=nd.gaussian_filter(l,18)
    out=pigment(190+(paper-174)*.22+fine*.16,19,40)
    nature=np.isin(bio,[3,4,5])
    if (ROOT/'base/painted_canopy_fine.png').exists():
        crown=np.asarray(Image.open(ROOT/'base/painted_canopy_fine.png').resize((n,n),Image.Resampling.NEAREST))>0
    else:
        # Pilot only. Final acceptance uses one frozen finest-scale canopy layer
        # for ALL zooms, including world data, rather than independent tree guesses.
        crown=((raw[...,1]-raw[...,0]>-5)&(raw[...,1]-raw[...,2]>30))|((raw[...,1]-raw[...,0]>-18)&(raw[...,1]-raw[...,2]>48)&(raw[...,1]<170))
        crown=nd.binary_closing(crown,iterations=1)
    nature=(nature|crown)&~(w|rd|b)
    green=raw.copy();green[...,1]=np.clip(150+(raw[...,1]-150)*.85,70,195)
    green[...,0]=green[...,1]+np.clip(raw[...,0]-raw[...,1],-8,12)
    green[...,2]=green[...,1]-np.clip(raw[...,1]-raw[...,2],46,66)
    out[nature]=green[nature]
    beach=bio==6
    out[beach]=pigment(211+(l-190)*.30,19,50)[beach]
    # Water is kept as generated watercolor, with exact coast repair.
    water=raw.copy()
    water[...,1]=np.maximum(water[...,1],water[...,0]+12)
    water[...,2]=np.maximum(water[...,2],water[...,0]+1)
    dw=nd.distance_transform_edt(w).astype(np.float32)
    # A continuous wet wash softens pigment extended across registration gaps.
    # Normalize inside water so nearby masonry never bleeds into the shallows.
    sigma=max(1.5,12/mpp)
    mf=w.astype(np.float32);den=nd.gaussian_filter(mf,sigma)
    blend=np.exp(-dw/max(2,48/mpp))*.85*w
    for k in range(3):
        wash=nd.gaussian_filter(water[...,k]*mf,sigma)/np.maximum(den,.001)
        water[...,k]=water[...,k]*(1-blend)+wash*blend
    out[w]=water[w]
    # Pale shallows and crisp ink at the measured water edge.
    # Hide nearest-pigment extension streaks with a continuous shallow wash.
    near=np.exp(-dw/max(2,32/mpp))*.72*w
    shallow=np.stack([153+fine*.15,181+fine*.15,165+fine*.15],-1)
    out=out*(1-near[...,None])+shallow*near[...,None]
    shore=w&(dw<=1)
    out[shore]=out[shore]*.40+np.array([45,72,63],np.float32)*.60
    landedge=(~w)&(nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)<=1)&~b&~rd
    out[landedge]*=.62
    # Exact road corridors, with economical shoulder lines, no invented lanes.
    rdist=nd.distance_transform_edt(rd).astype(np.float32)
    rl=211+np.clip((raw[...,1]-190)*.42,-28,18)+fine*.28
    if z>0:rl=rl-np.where(rdist<=1,22,0).astype(np.float32)
    out[rd]=pigment(rl,7,38)[rd]
    # Footprint-specific ruined masonry, preserving true courtyards and holes.
    db=nd.distance_transform_edt(b).astype(np.float32)
    bl=174+(soft-174)*.20+fine*.32 if z<2 else 174+(l-174)*.75+fine*.20
    if z==0:bl-=np.where(db<=1,43,0).astype(np.float32)
    else:bl-=np.where(db<=1,67,np.where(db<=2,10,0)).astype(np.float32)
    yy,xx=np.indices((n,n),dtype=np.int32)
    if z>=1:
        # Restrained quill hatch along interior walls; tied to map coordinates.
        hatch=((xx+yy*2)%(8+z)==0)&(db>1)&(db<4+z)
        bl[hatch]-=25
        # Unequal interior coursing; never spills beyond a building footprint.
        courses=((xx*3-yy)%19==0)&(db>3)
        bl[courses]-=10
    out[b]=pigment(bl,16,23)[b]
    # An explicit authored standing-water layer, not an extra invented coastline.
    flood=(grid_at('flooded_streets',n)>0)&rd&~b
    out[flood]=np.array([119,155,146])+fine[flood,None]*.2
    # Match broad pigment fields to accepted parent while retaining native detail.
    # Material-local luminance matching avoids smearing a coast into neighboring land.
    if z>0:
        parent_path=ROOT/'paintings'/f'z{z-1}'/'final-master.png'
        if not parent_path.exists():parent_path=ROOT/'checks'/f'partial_z{z-1}.png'
        parent=load(parent_path,(n,n))
        masks=[w,rd&~b&~flood,b,nature&~rd&~b,beach&~rd&~b,~(w|rd|b|nature|beach)]
        for mask in masks:

            den=nd.gaussian_filter(mf,12)
            a=nd.gaussian_filter(out[...,1]*mf,12)/np.maximum(den,.01)
            p=nd.gaussian_filter(parent[...,1]*mf,12)/np.maximum(den,.01)
            delta=np.clip(p-a,-50,50)*.96
            out[mask]+=delta[mask,None]

        mf=w.astype(np.float32);den=nd.gaussian_filter(mf,8)
        for k in [0,2]:
            a=nd.gaussian_filter(out[...,k]*mf,8)/np.maximum(den,.01)
            p=nd.gaussian_filter(parent[...,k]*mf,8)/np.maximum(den,.01)
            delta=np.clip(p-a,-55,55)

 The game tile images instead use pixel areas: at zoom z, pixel centers are `(−4064 +(column+.5)×8128/(1024×2^z), 4064−(row+.5)×8128/(1024×2^z))`. This distinction prevents a half-pixel drift.

+For screen coordinates on the north-up picture, use eastward `u = 100×(E+4064)/8128` and southward `v = 100×(4064−N)/8128`, where `(E,N)` are our local projected easting/northing. +## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
 
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+

+## Round two: scale and paper take priority
+
+The first finish lost the paper and forced all 11,919 footprints into every scale. The new overview and district originals use the same original style sheet with these stronger decisions:
+
+- **z0:** main avenues/causeways only; districts described by ivory intervals, loose wash and directional hatching. +- **Substrate:** exposed ivory, approximately #EDE1C6, with original rag tooth. The earlier land-wash anchor is a transparent pigment, never an opaque fill across all land. Quiet teal water may show paper tooth too.

+- **Narrative:** actual saved missing spans and flooded streets stay in the rendering. Symbols communicate the drowned district at far scales; exact corridors and open rooms take over close up. Never add cranes to residential islands or invented wrecks to empty water.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+"""Scale-legible wreck symbols at saved world positions, not enlarged world hulls."""
+import math
+from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
+from common import B, SIZE, vectors
+
+
+def wreck_symbols(im, z):
+    if z > 1:
+        return im
+    scale = 4
+    layer = Image.new('RGBA', (im.width*scale, im.height*scale))
+    d = ImageDraw.Draw(layer)
+    mpp = SIZE/im.width
+    for _, p in vectors('future_changes'):
+        if p['kind'] != 'submerged_wreck':
+            continue
+        cx = (p['center'][0]-B[0])/mpp
+        cy = (B[3]-p['center'][1])/mpp
+        angle = -math.radians(p['angle_degrees'])
+        length = max(p['length_m']/mpp, 14 if z == 0 else 18)
+        width = max(p['width_m']/mpp, 4.5 if z == 0 else 5.5)
+        def point(u, v):
+            x = u*length; y = v*width
+            return ((cx+x*math.cos(angle)-y*math.sin(angle))*scale,
+                    (cy+x*math.sin(angle)+y*math.cos(angle))*scale)
+        hull = [(-.5,0),(-.35,-.44),(.22,-.5),(.5,0),(.22,.5),(-.35,.44)]
+        d.polygon([point(*q) for q in hull], fill=(100,125,108,225))
+        # One torn gunwale, rusted stem and pale exposed frames.
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[:4]], fill=(74,76,53,242), width=3)
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[4:]+[hull[0]]], fill=(82,84,60,220), width=2)
+        for i, u in enumerate([-.29,-.13,.05,.23]):
+            d.line([point(u,-.34),point(u,.31 if i!=2 else .1)],
+                   fill=(205,197,153,238), width=2)
+        d.line([point(.18,0),point(.46,0)], fill=(137,104,62,245), width=3)
+    layer = layer.resize(im.size, Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
+    return Image.alpha_composite(im.convert('RGBA'),layer).convert('RGB')

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
 
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

 Offline source/art tools only. They add no dependency to the engine or its build.
 
+## Current delivery: round two
+
+The original geographic pipeline below remains authoritative for source layers. The current art finish is **round2.py**, followed by **round2_balance.py**. Do not use the old `finish.py` entry point to export the round-two delivery: its all-features-at-all-scales treatment is the artistic behavior replaced in this round. Its registration/overlap helpers are still used for the close original paintings.
+
+Saved originals are sufficient to reproduce the current artwork; no image calls or downloads are needed when the base vectors and PNGs are present:
+
+```sh
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/reference.py
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2_restore.py
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 0
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 1
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 2
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2.py finish 3
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2_balance.py
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/round2_measure.py
+tools/mapart/.venv/bin/python tools/mapart/audit.py
+```
+
+Close-tile registration additionally needs the native 64-pixel geometry contexts. `round2_restore.py` reconstructs these for z2/z3 without altering the historical used prompts; run it immediately after `reference.py`, as above. Contexts used for registration contain geometry, not the parent painting, so the generation-time parent is not needed to re-finish saved originals. The context-generation tools listed below are for commissioning new paintings and can overwrite prompts; they are not part of the reproduction sequence.
+
+| Round-two tool | Purpose |
+|---|---|
+| round2.py generalized 0 | Rebuild the overview's generalized plan from native vectors and spaced footprint anchors. The exact generation-time reference is also preserved as paintings/z0/geometry-input.png. |
+| round2.py contexts 1 | Prepare four generalized district references, parent crops and prompts for **new** image generation. Overwrites the z1 queue/prompts; not necessary for reproduction. |
+| round2_close_contexts.py | Prepare sixteen native neighborhood references and new district-parent crops; writes round2-queue.json. The accepted outputs replace z2 originals in place. |
+| round2.py finish Z | Continuous native canvas, scale-selected roads, geography-constrained coast, exposed rag paper, data-clipped architecture and district treatments. Keeps z3's original room paintings. Writes an ignored unbalanced-master.png and provisional final-master/tiles. |
+| round2_balance.py | Share broad RGB wash corrections across all four independent paintings without moving any ink geometry; cut final 1,024² tiles only after the continuous-canvas adjustment. |
+| round2_symbols.py | Called by the balance/export pass: draw legible z0/z1 wreck symbols at the four saved world positions and directions. Symbol size is not a new world footprint. |
+| round2_measure.py | All 140 separate tile joins, zero-loss reconstruction, adjacent-zoom RGB/8-pixel broad comparison, explicit limited pigment-boundary diagnostic, selected road support, and retained SHA-256 inventory. |
+| round2_restore.py | Recreate native registration contexts and review sheets from kept layers/originals/tiles. |
+
+Measurements, production notes and delivery audit are retained under `assets/source/maps/miami/reports/`, and interpreted in `REPORT.md`. `checks/` contains only regenerable review pictures, external comparison copies, and experiments. Raw downloads, references, warped copies and continuous finishing masters are ignored. No runtime/engine package or map file is produced.
+
+The built-in image tool was used for every new raster painting. Exact prompts are beside the originals. The corrected z1 northeast original also has a correction prompt and its preceding source under `paintings/z1/studies/`. The first new overview study is retained under `style/` because it supplied art direction to the accepted overview. Foreign comparison images were inspected only, never passed to image generation. Generation itself is nondeterministic; the saved originals make finishing reproducible.

+def assemble_far(z,w):
+    n=len(w);g=64;s=1152
+    out=np.zeros((n,n,3),np.float32);total=np.zeros((n,n),np.float32)
+    ramp=np.ones(s,np.float32);ramp[:128]=np.sin(np.linspace(0,np.pi/2,128))**2;ramp[-128:]=ramp[:128][::-1]
+    weight=ramp[:,None]*ramp[None,:];padded=np.pad(w,g,mode='edge')
+    for y in range(2**z):
+        for x in range(2**z):
+            p=ROOT/f'paintings/z{z}/{x}_{y}.raw.png'
+            a,info=far_register(load(p,(s,s)),padded[y*1024:y*1024+s,x*1024:x*1024+s])
+            p.with_name(f'{x}_{y}.registered.json').write_text(json.dumps(info,indent=2))
+            xa=max(0,x*1024-g);xb=min(n,(x+1)*1024+g);ya=max(0,y*1024-g);yb=min(n,(y+1)*1024+g)
+            u=xa-(x*1024-g);v=ya-(y*1024-g);q=weight[v:v+yb-ya,u:u+xb-xa]
+            out[ya:yb,xa:xb]+=a[v:v+yb-ya,u:u+xb-xa]*q[...,None];total[ya:yb,xa:xb]+=q
+    return out/np.maximum(total[...,None],1e-6)

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+"""Scale-legible wreck symbols at saved world positions, not enlarged world hulls."""
+import math
+from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
+from common import B, SIZE, vectors
+
+
+def wreck_symbols(im, z):
+    if z > 1:
+        return im
+    scale = 4
+    layer = Image.new('RGBA', (im.width*scale, im.height*scale))
+    d = ImageDraw.Draw(layer)
+    mpp = SIZE/im.width
+    for _, p in vectors('future_changes'):
+        if p['kind'] != 'submerged_wreck':
+            continue
+        cx = (p['center'][0]-B[0])/mpp
+        cy = (B[3]-p['center'][1])/mpp
+        angle = -math.radians(p['angle_degrees'])
+        length = max(p['length_m']/mpp, 14 if z == 0 else 18)
+        width = max(p['width_m']/mpp, 4.5 if z == 0 else 5.5)
+        def point(u, v):
+            x = u*length; y = v*width
+            return ((cx+x*math.cos(angle)-y*math.sin(angle))*scale,
+                    (cy+x*math.sin(angle)+y*math.cos(angle))*scale)
+        hull = [(-.5,0),(-.35,-.44),(.22,-.5),(.5,0),(.22,.5),(-.35,.44)]
+        d.polygon([point(*q) for q in hull], fill=(100,125,108,225))
+        # One torn gunwale, rusted stem and pale exposed frames.
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[:4]], fill=(74,76,53,242), width=3)
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[4:]+[hull[0]]], fill=(82,84,60,220), width=2)
+        for i, u in enumerate([-.29,-.13,.05,.23]):
+            d.line([point(u,-.34),point(u,.31 if i!=2 else .1)],
+                   fill=(205,197,153,238), width=2)
+        d.line([point(.18,0),point(.46,0)], fill=(137,104,62,245), width=3)
+    layer = layer.resize(im.size, Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
+    return Image.alpha_composite(im.convert('RGBA'),layer).convert('RGB')

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
 
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+"""Scale-legible wreck symbols at saved world positions, not enlarged world hulls."""
+import math
+from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
+from common import B, SIZE, vectors
+
+
+def wreck_symbols(im, z):
+    if z > 1:
+        return im
+    scale = 4
+    layer = Image.new('RGBA', (im.width*scale, im.height*scale))
+    d = ImageDraw.Draw(layer)
+    mpp = SIZE/im.width
+    for _, p in vectors('future_changes'):
+        if p['kind'] != 'submerged_wreck':
+            continue
+        cx = (p['center'][0]-B[0])/mpp
+        cy = (B[3]-p['center'][1])/mpp
+        angle = -math.radians(p['angle_degrees'])
+        length = max(p['length_m']/mpp, 14 if z == 0 else 18)
+        width = max(p['width_m']/mpp, 4.5 if z == 0 else 5.5)
+        def point(u, v):
+            x = u*length; y = v*width
+            return ((cx+x*math.cos(angle)-y*math.sin(angle))*scale,
+                    (cy+x*math.sin(angle)+y*math.cos(angle))*scale)
+        hull = [(-.5,0),(-.35,-.44),(.22,-.5),(.5,0),(.22,.5),(-.35,.44)]
+        d.polygon([point(*q) for q in hull], fill=(100,125,108,225))
+        # One torn gunwale, rusted stem and pale exposed frames.
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[:4]], fill=(74,76,53,242), width=3)
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[4:]+[hull[0]]], fill=(82,84,60,220), width=2)
+        for i, u in enumerate([-.29,-.13,.05,.23]):
+            d.line([point(u,-.34),point(u,.31 if i!=2 else .1)],
+                   fill=(205,197,153,238), width=2)
+        d.line([point(.18,0),point(.46,0)], fill=(137,104,62,245), width=3)
+    layer = layer.resize(im.size, Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
+    return Image.alpha_composite(im.convert('RGBA'),layer).convert('RGB')

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
 
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+"""Scale-legible wreck symbols at saved world positions, not enlarged world hulls."""
+import math
+from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
+from common import B, SIZE, vectors
+
+
+def wreck_symbols(im, z):
+    if z > 1:
+        return im
+    scale = 4
+    layer = Image.new('RGBA', (im.width*scale, im.height*scale))
+    d = ImageDraw.Draw(layer)
+    mpp = SIZE/im.width
+    for _, p in vectors('future_changes'):
+        if p['kind'] != 'submerged_wreck':
+            continue
+        cx = (p['center'][0]-B[0])/mpp
+        cy = (B[3]-p['center'][1])/mpp
+        angle = -math.radians(p['angle_degrees'])
+        length = max(p['length_m']/mpp, 14 if z == 0 else 18)
+        width = max(p['width_m']/mpp, 4.5 if z == 0 else 5.5)
+        def point(u, v):
+            x = u*length; y = v*width
+            return ((cx+x*math.cos(angle)-y*math.sin(angle))*scale,
+                    (cy+x*math.sin(angle)+y*math.cos(angle))*scale)
+        hull = [(-.5,0),(-.35,-.44),(.22,-.5),(.5,0),(.22,.5),(-.35,.44)]
+        d.polygon([point(*q) for q in hull], fill=(100,125,108,225))
+        # One torn gunwale, rusted stem and pale exposed frames.
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[:4]], fill=(74,76,53,242), width=3)
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[4:]+[hull[0]]], fill=(82,84,60,220), width=2)
+        for i, u in enumerate([-.29,-.13,.05,.23]):
+            d.line([point(u,-.34),point(u,.31 if i!=2 else .1)],
+                   fill=(205,197,153,238), width=2)
+        d.line([point(.18,0),point(.46,0)], fill=(137,104,62,245), width=3)
+    layer = layer.resize(im.size, Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
+    return Image.alpha_composite(im.convert('RGBA'),layer).convert('RGB')

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
 
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+"""Scale-legible wreck symbols at saved world positions, not enlarged world hulls."""
+import math
+from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
+from common import B, SIZE, vectors
+
+
+def wreck_symbols(im, z):
+    if z > 1:
+        return im
+    scale = 4
+    layer = Image.new('RGBA', (im.width*scale, im.height*scale))
+    d = ImageDraw.Draw(layer)
+    mpp = SIZE/im.width
+    for _, p in vectors('future_changes'):
+        if p['kind'] != 'submerged_wreck':
+            continue
+        cx = (p['center'][0]-B[0])/mpp
+        cy = (B[3]-p['center'][1])/mpp
+        angle = -math.radians(p['angle_degrees'])
+        length = max(p['length_m']/mpp, 14 if z == 0 else 18)
+        width = max(p['width_m']/mpp, 4.5 if z == 0 else 5.5)
+        def point(u, v):
+            x = u*length; y = v*width
+            return ((cx+x*math.cos(angle)-y*math.sin(angle))*scale,
+                    (cy+x*math.sin(angle)+y*math.cos(angle))*scale)
+        hull = [(-.5,0),(-.35,-.44),(.22,-.5),(.5,0),(.22,.5),(-.35,.44)]
+        d.polygon([point(*q) for q in hull], fill=(100,125,108,225))
+        # One torn gunwale, rusted stem and pale exposed frames.
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[:4]], fill=(74,76,53,242), width=3)
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[4:]+[hull[0]]], fill=(82,84,60,220), width=2)
+        for i, u in enumerate([-.29,-.13,.05,.23]):
+            d.line([point(u,-.34),point(u,.31 if i!=2 else .1)],
+                   fill=(205,197,153,238), width=2)
+        d.line([point(.18,0),point(.46,0)], fill=(137,104,62,245), width=3)
+    layer = layer.resize(im.size, Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
+    return Image.alpha_composite(im.convert('RGBA'),layer).convert('RGB')

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
 
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

 Never put lettering, a grid, compass, neatline, legend or page edge into a game tile. The separate style sheet may have sample captions. No mountainous relief: Miami is low and flat. No gratuitous noise or repeated decorative stamps.
+
+## Round two: scale and paper take priority
+
+The first finish lost the paper and forced all 11,919 footprints into every scale. The new overview and district originals use the same original style sheet with these stronger decisions:
+
+- **z0:** main avenues/causeways only; districts described by ivory intervals, loose wash and directional hatching. A small pictorial skyline, port sheds/cranes, courtyard ruins and beach hotels are representative district symbols. Their projected heights are illustrative; do not read a symbol's drawn silhouette as a surveyed building footprint.
+- **z1:** spaced source-building anchors and groups of ruins, more canals and park detail, still generous unpainted ground. Do not bring back the complete minor-road or house mesh.
+- **z2/z3:** the actual footprint fabric returns. Keep independently painted roofless rooms and vegetation; differentiate warehouse trusses, pale beach galleries, darker downtown masonry and low residential shells.
+- **Substrate:** exposed ivory, approximately #EDE1C6, with original rag tooth. The earlier land-wash anchor is a transparent pigment, never an opaque fill across all land. Quiet teal water may show paper tooth too.
+- **Coast:** a geographically constrained hand, with variable pressure, short pen lifts, doubled quay strokes, almost no outline across a beach, and coast-following jade shallows. Do not encode all materials into rigid RGB categories merely to obtain perfect colour-classification scores.
+- **Narrative:** actual saved missing spans and flooded streets stay in the rendering. Symbols communicate the drowned district at far scales; exact corridors and open rooms take over close up. Never add cranes to residential islands or invented wrecks to empty water.
+
+`paper-study.png` is the first round-two art direction study, retained because it was an input to the accepted overview. Its geometry is not authoritative. Its elastic finishing experiment was rejected for warping architecture. The production log records the subsequent corrections.

+|---|---|

+| round2_close_contexts.py | Prepare sixteen native neighborhood references and new district-parent crops; writes round2-queue.json. The accepted outputs replace z2 originals in place. |
+| round2.py finish Z | Continuous native canvas, scale-selected roads, geography-constrained coast, exposed rag paper, data-clipped architecture and district treatments. Keeps z3's original room paintings. Writes an ignored unbalanced-master.png and provisional final-master/tiles. |

+| round2_symbols.py | Called by the balance/export pass: draw legible z0/z1 wreck symbols at the four saved world positions and directions. Symbol size is not a new world footprint. |
+| round2_measure.py | All 140 separate tile joins, zero-loss reconstruction, adjacent-zoom RGB/8-pixel broad comparison, explicit limited pigment-boundary diagnostic, selected road support, and retained SHA-256 inventory. |
+| round2_restore.py | Recreate native registration contexts and review sheets from kept layers/originals/tiles. |

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+"""Scale-legible wreck symbols at saved world positions, not enlarged world hulls."""
+import math
+from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
+from common import B, SIZE, vectors
+
+
+def wreck_symbols(im, z):
+    if z > 1:
+        return im
+    scale = 4
+    layer = Image.new('RGBA', (im.width*scale, im.height*scale))
+    d = ImageDraw.Draw(layer)
+    mpp = SIZE/im.width
+    for _, p in vectors('future_changes'):
+        if p['kind'] != 'submerged_wreck':
+            continue
+        cx = (p['center'][0]-B[0])/mpp
+        cy = (B[3]-p['center'][1])/mpp
+        angle = -math.radians(p['angle_degrees'])
+        length = max(p['length_m']/mpp, 14 if z == 0 else 18)
+        width = max(p['width_m']/mpp, 4.5 if z == 0 else 5.5)
+        def point(u, v):
+            x = u*length; y = v*width
+            return ((cx+x*math.cos(angle)-y*math.sin(angle))*scale,
+                    (cy+x*math.sin(angle)+y*math.cos(angle))*scale)
+        hull = [(-.5,0),(-.35,-.44),(.22,-.5),(.5,0),(.22,.5),(-.35,.44)]
+        d.polygon([point(*q) for q in hull], fill=(100,125,108,225))
+        # One torn gunwale, rusted stem and pale exposed frames.
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[:4]], fill=(74,76,53,242), width=3)
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[4:]+[hull[0]]], fill=(82,84,60,220), width=2)
+        for i, u in enumerate([-.29,-.13,.05,.23]):
+            d.line([point(u,-.34),point(u,.31 if i!=2 else .1)],
+                   fill=(205,197,153,238), width=2)
+        d.line([point(.18,0),point(.46,0)], fill=(137,104,62,245), width=3)
+    layer = layer.resize(im.size, Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
+    return Image.alpha_composite(im.convert('RGBA'),layer).convert('RGB')

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
 
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+

This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

The context-generation tools listed below are for commissioning new paintings and can overwrite prompts; they are not part of the reproduction sequence.
+
+| Round-two tool | Purpose |
+|---|---|
+| round2.py generalized 0 | Rebuild the overview's generalized plan from native vectors and spaced footprint anchors. The exact generation-time reference is also preserved as paintings/z0/geometry-input.png. |
+| round2.py contexts 1 | Prepare four generalized district references, parent crops and prompts for **new** image generation. Overwrites the z1 queue/prompts; not necessary for reproduction. |
+| round2_close_contexts.py | Prepare sixteen native neighborhood references and new district-parent crops; writes round2-queue.json. The accepted outputs replace z2 originals in place. |
+| round2.py finish Z | Continuous native canvas, scale-selected roads, geography-constrained coast, exposed rag paper, data-clipped architecture and district treatments. Keeps z3's original room paintings. Writes an ignored unbalanced-master.png and provisional final-master/tiles. |
+| round2_balance.py | Share broad RGB wash corrections across all four independent paintings without moving any ink geometry; cut final 1,024² tiles only after the continuous-canvas adjustment. |
+| round2_symbols.py | Called by the balance/export pass: draw legible z0/z1 wreck symbols at the four saved world positions and directions. Symbol size is not a new world footprint. |
+| round2_measure.py | All 140 separate tile joins, zero-loss reconstruction, adjacent-zoom RGB/8-pixel broad comparison, explicit limited pigment-boundary diagnostic, selected road support, and retained SHA-256 inventory. |
+| round2_restore.py | Recreate native registration contexts and review sheets from kept layers/originals/tiles. |
+
+Measurements, production notes and delivery audit are retained under `assets/source/maps/miami/reports/`, and interpreted in `REPORT.md`. `checks/` contains only regenerable review pictures, external comparison copies, and experiments. Raw downloads, references, warped copies and continuous finishing masters are ignored. No runtime/engine package or map file is produced.
+
+The built-in image tool was used for every new raster painting. Exact prompts are beside the originals. The corrected z1 northeast original also has a correction prompt and its preceding source under `paintings/z1/studies/`. The first new overview study is retained under `style/` because it supplied art direction to the accepted overview. Foreign comparison images were inspected only, never passed to image generation. Generation itself is nondeterministic; the saved originals make finishing reproducible.
+
+## Original geographic preparation and round-one tools
+

+def assemble_far(z,w):
+    n=len(w);g=64;s=1152
+    out=np.zeros((n,n,3),np.float32);total=np.zeros((n,n),np.float32)
+    ramp=np.ones(s,np.float32);ramp[:128]=np.sin(np.linspace(0,np.pi/2,128))**2;ramp[-128:]=ramp[:128][::-1]
+    weight=ramp[:,None]*ramp[None,:];padded=np.pad(w,g,mode='edge')
+    for y in range(2**z):
+        for x in range(2**z):
+            p=ROOT/f'paintings/z{z}/{x}_{y}.raw.png'
+            a,info=far_register(load(p,(s,s)),padded[y*1024:y*1024+s,x*1024:x*1024+s])
+            p.with_name(f'{x}_{y}.registered.json').write_text(json.dumps(info,indent=2))
+            xa=max(0,x*1024-g);xb=min(n,(x+1)*1024+g);ya=max(0,y*1024-g);yb=min(n,(y+1)*1024+g)
+            u=xa-(x*1024-g);v=ya-(y*1024-g);q=weight[v:v+yb-ya,u:u+xb-xa]
+            out[ya:yb,xa:xb]+=a[v:v+yb-ya,u:u+xb-xa]*q[...,None];total[ya:yb,xa:xb]+=q
+    return out/np.maximum(total[...,None],1e-6)

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+"""Scale-legible wreck symbols at saved world positions, not enlarged world hulls."""
+import math
+from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
+from common import B, SIZE, vectors
+
+
+def wreck_symbols(im, z):
+    if z > 1:
+        return im
+    scale = 4
+    layer = Image.new('RGBA', (im.width*scale, im.height*scale))
+    d = ImageDraw.Draw(layer)
+    mpp = SIZE/im.width
+    for _, p in vectors('future_changes'):
+        if p['kind'] != 'submerged_wreck':
+            continue
+        cx = (p['center'][0]-B[0])/mpp
+        cy = (B[3]-p['center'][1])/mpp
+        angle = -math.radians(p['angle_degrees'])
+        length = max(p['length_m']/mpp, 14 if z == 0 else 18)
+        width = max(p['width_m']/mpp, 4.5 if z == 0 else 5.5)
+        def point(u, v):
+            x = u*length; y = v*width
+            return ((cx+x*math.cos(angle)-y*math.sin(angle))*scale,
+                    (cy+x*math.sin(angle)+y*math.cos(angle))*scale)
+        hull = [(-.5,0),(-.35,-.44),(.22,-.5),(.5,0),(.22,.5),(-.35,.44)]
+        d.polygon([point(*q) for q in hull], fill=(100,125,108,225))
+        # One torn gunwale, rusted stem and pale exposed frames.
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[:4]], fill=(74,76,53,242), width=3)
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[4:]+[hull[0]]], fill=(82,84,60,220), width=2)
+        for i, u in enumerate([-.29,-.13,.05,.23]):
+            d.line([point(u,-.34),point(u,.31 if i!=2 else .1)],
+                   fill=(205,197,153,238), width=2)
+        d.line([point(.18,0),point(.46,0)], fill=(137,104,62,245), width=3)
+    layer = layer.resize(im.size, Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
+    return Image.alpha_composite(im.convert('RGBA'),layer).convert('RGB')

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
 
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)

+"""Scale-legible wreck symbols at saved world positions, not enlarged world hulls."""
+import math
+from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
+from common import B, SIZE, vectors
+
+
+def wreck_symbols(im, z):
+    if z > 1:
+        return im
+    scale = 4
+    layer = Image.new('RGBA', (im.width*scale, im.height*scale))
+    d = ImageDraw.Draw(layer)
+    mpp = SIZE/im.width
+    for _, p in vectors('future_changes'):
+        if p['kind'] != 'submerged_wreck':
+            continue
+        cx = (p['center'][0]-B[0])/mpp
+        cy = (B[3]-p['center'][1])/mpp
+        angle = -math.radians(p['angle_degrees'])
+        length = max(p['length_m']/mpp, 14 if z == 0 else 18)
+        width = max(p['width_m']/mpp, 4.5 if z == 0 else 5.5)
+        def point(u, v):
+            x = u*length; y = v*width
+            return ((cx+x*math.cos(angle)-y*math.sin(angle))*scale,
+                    (cy+x*math.sin(angle)+y*math.cos(angle))*scale)
+        hull = [(-.5,0),(-.35,-.44),(.22,-.5),(.5,0),(.22,.5),(-.35,.44)]
+        d.polygon([point(*q) for q in hull], fill=(100,125,108,225))
+        # One torn gunwale, rusted stem and pale exposed frames.
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[:4]], fill=(74,76,53,242), width=3)
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[4:]+[hull[0]]], fill=(82,84,60,220), width=2)
+        for i, u in enumerate([-.29,-.13,.05,.23]):
+            d.line([point(u,-.34),point(u,.31 if i!=2 else .1)],
+                   fill=(205,197,153,238), width=2)
+        d.line([point(.18,0),point(.46,0)], fill=(137,104,62,245), width=3)
+    layer = layer.resize(im.size, Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
+    return Image.alpha_composite(im.convert('RGBA'),layer).convert('RGB')

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
 
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.
+

+## Round two: scale and paper take priority
+
+The first finish lost the paper and forced all 11,919 footprints into every scale. The new overview and district originals use the same original style sheet with these stronger decisions:
+
+- **z0:** main avenues/causeways only; districts described by ivory intervals, loose wash and directional hatching. A small pictorial skyline, port sheds/cranes, courtyard ruins and beach hotels are representative district symbols. Their projected heights are illustrative; do not read a symbol's drawn silhouette as a surveyed building footprint.
+- **z1:** spaced source-building anchors and groups of ruins, more canals and park detail, still generous unpainted ground. Do not bring back the complete minor-road or house mesh.
+- **z2/z3:** the actual footprint fabric returns. Keep independently painted roofless rooms and vegetation; differentiate warehouse trusses, pale beach galleries, darker downtown masonry and low residential shells.
+- **Substrate:** exposed ivory, approximately #EDE1C6, with original rag tooth. The earlier land-wash anchor is a transparent pigment, never an opaque fill across all land. Quiet teal water may show paper tooth too.
+- **Coast:** a geographically constrained hand, with variable pressure, short pen lifts, doubled quay strokes, almost no outline across a beach, and coast-following jade shallows. Do not encode all materials into rigid RGB categories merely to obtain perfect colour-classification scores.
+- **Narrative:** actual saved missing spans and flooded streets stay in the rendering. Symbols communicate the drowned district at far scales; exact corridors and open rooms take over close up. Never add cranes to residential islands or invented wrecks to empty water.

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw

+"""Scale-legible wreck symbols at saved world positions, not enlarged world hulls."""
+import math
+from PIL import Image, ImageDraw
+from common import B, SIZE, vectors

+def wreck_symbols(im, z):
+    if z > 1:
+        return im
+    scale = 4
+    layer = Image.new('RGBA', (im.width*scale, im.height*scale))
+    d = ImageDraw.Draw(layer)
+    mpp = SIZE/im.width
+    for _, p in vectors('future_changes'):
+        if p['kind'] != 'submerged_wreck':
+            continue
+        cx = (p['center'][0]-B[0])/mpp
+        cy = (B[3]-p['center'][1])/mpp
+        angle = -math.radians(p['angle_degrees'])
+        length = max(p['length_m']/mpp, 14 if z == 0 else 18)
+        width = max(p['width_m']/mpp, 4.5 if z == 0 else 5.5)
+        def point(u, v):
+            x = u*length; y = v*width
+            return ((cx+x*math.cos(angle)-y*math.sin(angle))*scale,
+                    (cy+x*math.sin(angle)+y*math.cos(angle))*scale)
+        hull = [(-.5,0),(-.35,-.44),(.22,-.5),(.5,0),(.22,.5),(-.35,.44)]
+        d.polygon([point(*q) for q in hull], fill=(100,125,108,225))
+        # One torn gunwale, rusted stem and pale exposed frames.
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[:4]], fill=(74,76,53,242), width=3)
+        d.line([point(*q) for q in hull[4:]+[hull[0]]], fill=(82,84,60,220), width=2)
+        for i, u in enumerate([-.29,-.13,.05,.23]):
+            d.line([point(u,-.34),point(u,.31 if i!=2 else .1)],
+                   fill=(205,197,153,238), width=2)
+        d.line([point(.18,0),point(.46,0)], fill=(137,104,62,245), width=3)
+    layer = layer.resize(im.size, Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
+    return Image.alpha_composite(im.convert('RGBA'),layer).convert('RGB')

+## Exact conversion to the engine (checked for round two)
+
+Checked against [Maps as files](../../../../../planning/reference/maps.md), section “A folder of layers”, and the input contract and reader used by [tools/map.ts](../../../../../tools/map.ts). The engine origin is the **south-east** corner; **+x is west**, **+z is north**, and +y is height. Our vectors use east-positive `(E,N)` metres from the centre. Convert positions as follows, without swapping the axes:
+
+```text
+engine.x = 4064 - E
+engine.z = 4064 + N
+engine.y = elevation_metres
 
+E = 4064 - engine.x
+N = engine.z - 4064
+```
+
+| Point | Our (E,N), metres | Engine (x,z), metres |
+|---|---|---|
+| NW | (−4064,+4064) | (8128,8128) |
+| NE | (+4064,+4064) | (0,8128) |
+| SE, engine origin | (+4064,−4064) | (0,0) |
+| SW | (−4064,−4064) | (8128,0) |
+| Centre | (0,0) | (4064,4064) |
+
+Thus our 4,065² north-up sample `(column,row)` maps to `x = 8128−2×column`, `z = 8128−2×row`. **Do not mirror the PNGs before giving them to the layer importer**: its north-up contract already places the upper-left pixel at maximum x and maximum z. For a tile image with whole-map side `P=1024×2^zoom`, pixel centre `(c,r)` maps to `x=8128×(1−(c+0.5)/P)`, `z=8128×(1−(r+0.5)/P)`. Tile columns still increase eastward on screen, so engine x decreases as the tile column increases.
+
+Engine yaw starts at north and turns toward west (+x). For a projected direction `(dE,dN)`, use `yaw = atan2(−dE,dN)×180/π mod 360`: north 0°, west 90°, south 180°, east 270°. A vector angle θ measured counterclockwise from projected east, as in `future_changes.geojson`, becomes `(θ−90°) mod 360`. The horizontal transform is a reflection (determinant −1), so polygon ring winding reverses if transforming vertices; preserve/recompute exterior/hole semantics rather than interpreting the old winding blindly.
+
+Height values remain `value/100−100` metres NAVD88. The example engine height encoding is different; a later world builder must decode these heights and re-encode using its chosen `minY`/`stepY`. This note does not create an engine map file, choose version-2 fields, or assert a sea-level datum conversion.

 `areawater.geojson`, `roads.geojson` and `buildings.geojson` retain clipped vector geometry in the **local projected CRS**, not RFC 7946 geographic degrees. Their `crs` member declares it. Use them to render reference images afresh at every zoom. Do not enlarge the 2 m masks for close-scale shoreline tracing.

+## Round two: scale and paper take priority
+
+The first finish lost the paper and forced all 11,919 footprints into every scale. The new overview and district originals use the same original style sheet with these stronger decisions:
+
+- **z0:** main avenues/causeways only; districts described by ivory intervals, loose wash and directional hatching. A small pictorial skyline, port sheds/cranes, courtyard ruins and beach hotels are representative district symbols. Their projected heights are illustrative; do not read a symbol's drawn silhouette as a surveyed building footprint.
+- **z1:** spaced source-building anchors and groups of ruins, more canals and park detail, still generous unpainted ground. Do not bring back the complete minor-road or house mesh.
+- **z2/z3:** the actual footprint fabric returns. Keep independently painted roofless rooms and vegetation; differentiate warehouse trusses, pale beach galleries, darker downtown masonry and low residential shells.
+- **Substrate:** exposed ivory, approximately #EDE1C6, with original rag tooth. The earlier land-wash anchor is a transparent pigment, never an opaque fill across all land. Quiet teal water may show paper tooth too.
+- **Coast:** a geographically constrained hand, with variable pressure, short pen lifts, doubled quay strokes, almost no outline across a beach, and coast-following jade shallows. Do not encode all materials into rigid RGB categories merely to obtain perfect colour-classification scores.
+- **Narrative:** actual saved missing spans and flooded streets stay in the rendering. Symbols communicate the drowned district at far scales; exact corridors and open rooms take over close up. Never add cranes to residential islands or invented wrecks to empty water.
+
+`paper-study.png` is the first round-two art direction study, retained because it was an input to the accepted overview. Its geometry is not authoritative. Its elastic finishing experiment was rejected for warping architecture. The production log records the subsequent corrections.

+| round2_symbols.py | Called by the balance/export pass: draw legible z0/z1 wreck symbols at the four saved world positions and directions. Symbol size is not a new world footprint. |
+| round2_measure.py | All 140 separate tile joins, zero-loss reconstruction, adjacent-zoom RGB/8-pixel broad comparison, explicit limited pigment-boundary diagnostic, selected road support, and retained SHA-256 inventory. |
+| round2_restore.py | Recreate native registration contexts and review sheets from kept layers/originals/tiles. |

+def clean_far_coast(raw,w):
+    """Remove displaced source shore marks before drawing the measured shore.
+
+    Unlike unrestricted elastic registration this cannot bend architectural ink.
+    Only a narrow band beside source and target coasts is repainted.
+    """
+    sw=wet(raw)
+    # Ignore fine paper grain and ink pinholes when finding the painted coast.
+    sw=nd.binary_closing(sw,iterations=2,border_value=1)
+    sw=nd.binary_opening(sw,iterations=2)
+    ds=nd.distance_transform_edt(sw)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~sw)
+    dt=nd.distance_transform_edt(w)-nd.distance_transform_edt(~w)
+    displaced=(np.abs(ds)<3.5)&(np.abs(dt)<28)&(np.abs(dt)>2)
+    clean=cv2.inpaint(np.uint8(np.clip(raw,0,255)),displaced.astype('uint8'),5,cv2.INPAINT_TELEA).astype(np.float32)
+    landgood=(~sw)&(~w)&(raw.mean(2)>130)
+    den=nd.gaussian_filter(landgood.astype(np.float32),8)
+    bad=(~w)&sw&(np.abs(dt)<28)
+    for k in range(3):
+        field=nd.gaussian_filter(clean[...,k]*landgood,8)/np.maximum(den,.001)
+        field=np.where(den>.01,field,PAPER[k])
+        clean[...,k][bad]=field[bad]
+    return clean,sw
